The authors work with Gamma-convergence, which tracks limits of minimizing problems. They give an integral form for the limit energies. Those limits are free discontinuity functionals on a space of generalized functions of bounded variation. They also describe the bulk and surface densities of the limits. Each density comes from a minimization problem on small cubes for the approximating energies.
arxiv-2603-24492: Kratsch presents a faster algorithm for the Hamiltonian cycle problem when the input graph has small treedepth. Classic dynamic programming on tree decompositions is fast but uses exponential space, which fails for larger widths. Treedepth offers a stricter structure that can allow polynomial space with similar time bounds. Earlier work solved Hamiltonian cycle in about 5-to-the-tau time with a randomised method. Kratsch improves that running time while keeping polynomial space, using an elimination forest of the graph as the guiding structure.
arxiv-2603-24692: Cai and co-authors rebuild spiking neural networks using a single neuron with autapses. High-performing spiking models usually need dense multilayer designs with heavy memory costs. Their time-delayed autapse framework uses one leaky integrate-and-fire neuron plus prototype training. By reorganising internal states, it can realise reservoir, perceptron, and convolution-like designs in one scheme. Tests on sequential, event-based, and image benchmarks show competitive results. Neuron count and memory drop sharply, at the cost of extra latency in the single-neuron case.
arxiv-2603-25292: Devdutt, Garg, and Chatterjee derive the area spectrum of a black hole horizon when gravity couples to a scalar field in a non-minimal way. Entropy counts in quantum gravity rest on such microstate spectra. They use the weak isolated horizon frame. The spectrum falls straight out of the horizon symmetry algebra, with no full quantum gravity theory assumed. Steps come out evenly spaced, as the Bekenstein-Mukhanov idea suggests. The spacing depends on the Barbero-Immirzi value and the scalar field's strength at the horizon.
arxiv-2603-25792: Pinsonneault and co-authors announce the public release of the YREC stellar evolution code. YREC models brown dwarfs and stars across a wide mass range. It follows them from before the main sequence through helium burning. The release sums up the code's key ingredients and records how it performs. It also lists the code's strengths and limits. Libraries of input files, docs, sample cases, and scripts come with it. The authors note that the code suits teaching as well as research.
arxiv-2603-26192: Zhang and co-authors formalize lifelong learning across tasks with different output shapes. Most lifelong work assumes a stream of like tasks, such as classification only. Their setting, lifelong heterogeneous learning, mixes task types over time. They test it on dense prediction tasks. Their method, HAD, keeps old knowledge by self-distillation in each new phase. One loss balances the prediction spread across tasks. Another focuses on sharp edge pixels from the Sobel operator. The method needs no stored examples and beats prior methods, the authors report.
arxiv-2603-26292: Vázquez Martínez introduces findsylls, a toolkit for splitting speech into syllables in any language. Syllable units are compact and carry clear language value, but past tools vary in design and tests. The toolkit unifies classic detectors and end-to-end syllabifiers under one interface. Users can segment speech, pull embeddings, and score results at several levels. Trials cover English and Spanish, plus new hand-marked data from Kono, a little-documented Central Mande language.
arxiv-2603-26492: Schemeil studies the tensor-triangular geometry of motives generated by real quadrics. He works in Voevodsky's category of motives and focuses on the prime 2. There he determines the Balmer spectrum of the category. The spectrum turns out to be a countably infinite, non-Noetherian space of Krull dimension 2. He maps how it relates to the real Artin-Tate spectrum and to Vishik's isotropic points. Joining his result with known Artin-Tate work gives a full account of integral motives of quadrics over real algebraic numbers.
arxiv-2603-26692: Dzhafarov and Cervantes introduce contextuality profiles, a richer way to describe how contextual a system of random variables is. A single number flattens the picture, they argue. Their profile is a curve that ties the degree of contextuality to the level at which the system is viewed. At level n, only joint distributions over at most n variables count. The level-wise view works with any sound contextuality measure. A method of joined systems lets them trace profiles for three leading measures in the field.
arxiv-2603-26792: Bechir and co-authors adapt the Firefly Algorithm to optimisation problems that mix continuous, ordered, and category variables. Most swarm methods handle only one variable kind well, leaving mixed spaces awkward. Their FAmv version rebuilds the attraction rule around a hybrid distance. The distance joins numeric gaps and category matches in one formula, keeping search balanced between exploring and refining. On the CEC2013 mixed-variable benchmark it matches or beats leading rivals. Engineering design tests add support for its robustness in practice.
arxiv-2603-26892: Berg and co-authors compute one-loop graviton amplitudes using string-based methods. The target is half-maximal four-point amplitudes at one loop. Infrared divergences are tamed much as in soft-collinear effective theory. New mass scales enter through higher-point kinematics, keeping the integrals finite. A single-valued polylogarithm serves as the generating function for the results. The team provides code as a step toward automated amplitude calculations. The approach links string techniques to practical field theory tools.
arxiv-2603-27492: Li and co-authors decode hand motion from brain signals to drive a robot hand. Their model blends convolution layers with attention blocks. It reads EEG traces from grasp-and-lift tasks. Adding muscle signals through EMG lifts scores a great deal. Within-person tests reach correlations near 0.99 on two axes. Cross-person tests stay strong on those same axes. Decoded paths steer a Franka Panda arm in simulation. A copilot filter drops low-trust points to clean the path.
arxiv-2603-27692: Matheron and co-authors report a new way to focus high-energy beams. Dense beams drive lab astrophysics and strong-field studies. Magnet stacks are bulky and limit tight focus. At SLAC's FACET-II, a beam met a stack of thin foils. Its own magnetic field reflected off the foils. That reflection focused the beam strongly. The effect grew across many beam settings. Analytic and simulation results match the data. The method is simple and self-aligned.
arxiv-2603-27792: Schlegel and Seidl survey what-if tools for time series classifiers. Counterfactuals show the smallest change that flips a verdict. Their review spans neighbor, pattern, gradient, and generative methods. Each family is matched to its target models and data. Time data add hurdles absent in tables or images. Paths must stay coherent, plausible, and actionable. Strengths and limits are weighed on key axes. An open library, CFTS, anchors the comparisons.
arxiv-2603-28092: Yang and six co-authors propose InkDrop, a stealthier backdoor attack on dataset condensation. Condensed datasets can hide triggers that force wrong labels on chosen inputs, but past attacks were easy to spot. InkDrop picks samples near a decision boundary that already lean toward the target class. It then learns small per-sample changes that respect look and layout. Tests show the attack stays effective and keeps model utility, while drawing far less attention.
arxiv-2603-28392: Graham, Jeon, and Larson study orbit closures of a symmetric subgroup on the flag variety, a geometry tied to the representation theory of U(p,q). They resolve these closures with small resolutions whose fibers are smooth and strongly reduced. A general theorem then forces the characteristic cycle to be irreducible. From that, plus a result of Jones, they compute the torus-equivariant Chern-Mather classes. They conjecture these classes stay positive in the Schubert basis and check one case.
arxiv-2603-28492: Sakowska and six co-authors announce Andromeda XXXVI, a new ultra-faint dwarf galaxy near Andromeda. Deep images from the Gran Telescopio Canarias show a clean red giant branch in its color-magnitude diagram. The stars match an old, metal-poor population at Andromeda's distance of 776 kiloparsecs. The galaxy shines at magnitude -5.9 and spans about 64 parsecs, among the faintest Andromeda satellites known. Its existence hints at many more dim companions still hidden.
arxiv-2603-28692: Hedgepeth and co-authors model quantum optomechanical STIRAP for two mechanical modes coupled to an optical mode. STIRAP here means Stimulated Raman Adiabatic Passage. In a lossless system, they show that fractional STIRAP can create a mechanical Bell state. The starting point is a single phonon Fock state in one mode, with the other mode empty. Final phases depend on the parity of the starting phonon number. Numerical work adds dissipation to the picture. High-fidelity entanglement still seems possible with current cryogenic devices.
arxiv-2603-29292: Zhang and co-authors present ConSelf, a way for code models to improve without a teacher or test oracle. Fine-tuning usually needs costly external help. Their first tool is code semantic entropy. It measures how varied the behaviors of sampled programs are. That score builds a curriculum of the most learnable problems. Their second tool weights preference pairs by behavioral consensus. Noisy self-made supervision then does less damage. Experiments show gains over baselines on several benchmarks.
arxiv-2603-29892: Jaff and Mohammadamini extend the FLEURS speech benchmark to Northern Kurdish. FLEURS covers over 100 languages but lacked this Kurdish variety. Their FLEURS-Kobani set holds 5,162 checked utterances, about 18.5 hours in total. Thirty-one native speakers recorded the material. Fine-tuning Whisper v3-large in two stages gives the best speech recognition scores. Word error rate lands at 28.11 on the test set. They also report speech translation baselines into English.
arxiv-2604-00192: Alessandro Bravetti, García Ariza, and Romero-Arias extend the gradient-flow-pregeodesic link from dually flat manifolds to general Riemannian settings. Their result needs no flatness of the connection and no symmetry of its non-metricity tensor, widening the setting beyond Hessian manifolds. Within this framework, they give a criterion for comparing relaxation along two gradient descent curves, stated through the non-metricity tensor. Applied to Gaussian chains, whose relaxation paths match gradient descent curves, the work recovers a universal asymmetry: warming up runs faster than cooling down.
arxiv-2604-00292: Kumar and three colleagues build MambaVoiceCloning, a text-to-speech system whose conditioning runs entirely on state-space models at inference, with no attention or recurrent layers. A gated two-way Mamba text encoder, a Temporal Bi-Mamba guided by a throwaway alignment teacher, and an Expressive Mamba with modulation give linear-time conditioning, bounded memory, and streaming. Against StyleTTS2, VITS, and hybrid rivals, it wins modest but reliable gains on quality, pitch, and word error, while cutting encoder size to 21 million parameters and raising throughput 1.6 times.
arxiv-2604-00692: Xie and Zhang prove a quantitative diffusion approximation, uniform in time, for the joint law of fully coupled multiscale random systems. The limit law mixes the fast process's conditional equilibrium with the slow part's homogenized law. That gives a rigorous form of adiabatic elimination. Their rate separates fast early settling from slow long-time change, and they pin down the limit steady distribution and prove the two limits commute.
arxiv-2604-01192:
Simon Becker and two co-authors build a way to sample quantum heat states in a 2026 paper. Their frame is strict, can be built, and has no size cap. Heat states guide much work on how quantum systems settle down.

Past work of this kind was capped at small, finite size. Lifting that cap brings hard blocks, as the authors set out. The rules for the sampler can fail to make sense at large size. The spaces used may lack the gaps that make proofs of speed work. What can be built and what can be proved also pull apart. Their frame deals with how states are made, how fast they mix, and how to build the circuit. It fits systems such as springs and fields, which have no size cap by nature.
arxiv-2604-01492: Jackson and colleagues consider voidiness, the fraction of sight lines in voids, and its effect on photon propagation. A study showed Fermi LAT-detected active galactic nuclei lie along voidier lines of sight than matched Sloan quasars. They find line-of-sight interactions raising flux per Mpc of void traversed may suffice to explain the voidiness difference. They measure 28 percent of gamma-ray detected sources within a void, versus SDSS quasars. The voidiness difference may be due to line-of-sight interactions rather than the local environment.
arxiv-2604-01792: Patil and colleagues quantify how seasonal tomato price patterns in Kolar market drift year to year, using weekly prices and arrivals from 2010 to 2024. Statistics confirm wild swings, with variation of 77 percent for prices and 102 percent for arrivals, plus skew and heavy tails marking extremes. Seasonal indices show recurring yearly cycles, but alignment varies. Dynamic Time Warping for 2021 to 2024 finds the strongest alignment in 2022-2023 despite price spikes, and the weakest in 2021-2022, amid shifts. Seasonal patterns recur yet shift in time, so forecasts must adapt to magnitude swings and timing shifts.
arxiv-2604-01992: Maex builds integral and log cotangent complexes for extensions of valued fields, finite or purely transcendental. He constructs them from a MacLane Vaquie chain approximating the extension, yielding explicit formulas for the different, the weight norm and the Kahler norm. The methods give strong control over higher homology of the complexes, extending a key result of Gabber and Ramero into the logarithmic setting. The work turns abstract chain data into concrete invariants for valued field extensions.
arxiv-2604-02092: Patey and Shafer study a bounded twist on Ramsey theory for triples, where homogeneous sets in one color stay bounded in size. They show its computational content sits very close to Ramsey theory for pairs, matching the known upper bounds for pairs. Yet the triple version does not reduce computably to the pair version, even allowing repeated applications. The work thus places a restricted triple principle beside, but strictly above, its pair cousin in computational strength.
arxiv-2604-02192: Rybicki and colleagues ask what anonymous networks can compute when nodes lack IDs and merely broadcast to neighbors. In the weak SB and MB models, they give a one round deterministic algorithm that assigns unique IDs with high probability on random graphs. The method borrows from canonical labeling in graph isomorphism testing and can anonymize existing broadcast algorithms. They also find a triangle finding algorithm and show the weak model hierarchy collapses on these graphs, with SB nearly matching LOCAL.
arxiv-2604-02492: Choi and five colleagues introduce Image Prompt Packaging, a way to cut the cost of running large multimodal models. It writes structured text directly into images instead of feeding it as text tokens. Across five datasets, three leading models and two task types, the method cuts inference cost by 35.8 to 91.0 percent. Accuracy stays competitive in many settings, though results vary sharply by model and task.
arxiv-2604-02592: Li and Bakker run the first field evaluation of language-model fact-checking live on a social platform, through the AI writer feature of X Community Notes across three months. Their pipeline, which handles multimodal posts and searches the web and the platform, wrote 1,614 notes on 1,597 tweets, judged against 1,332 human notes through 108,169 ratings from 42,521 raters. Rating-level analysis shows the AI notes earning more positive ratings than human ones.
arxiv-2604-02892: Malvezzi and four colleagues introduce RAGE, a real-time estimator of tire grip for self-driving race cars using standard sensors like IMUs and radars. Traditional grip measurement needs costly special sensors with custom installation. RAGE infers vehicle velocity, tire slip angles, and lateral forces in one pass. Grip estimates let race cars run safely at their physical limits. Tests span high-fidelity simulations and real-world runs on the EAV-24 autonomous race car, showing accurate lateral dynamics estimation.
arxiv-2604-02992: Thiel and five colleagues survey 606 data analysts to learn why regularization, a standard guard against overfitting, sees uneven use. Written recommendations of regularization methods show no effect on trust or intended use in a randomized experiment. Instead, analysts adopt methods they find easy to implement and practically useful, for example for bias control or interpretability. Perceived social norms drive adoption strongly too. Uptake thus hinges less on formal advice than on usability, perceived benefit, and community practice.
arxiv-2604-03092: Zhang and colleagues speed up single-camera 3D mapping built from Gaussian splatting, which normally relearns the scene frame by frame. Their Flash-Mono system predicts camera poses and surface blobs directly from several frames at once, reusing a compact hidden state to close loops and correct drift. Tests show a tenfold speedup with top tracking and mapping quality, pointing toward live reconstruction for embodied robots.
arxiv-2604-03192: Sumit and colleagues study how to distill several teachers into one summarizer for low-resource Bangla text, gating supervision by how much teachers agree. Their reliability-aware methods route each token between teacher and gold guidance, and tests across Bangla datasets show logit-level distillation gives the most reliable gains. They also find single-judge evaluation carries calibration bias, unlike multi-judge checks.
arxiv-2604-03892: Miroslav Krstic and team used neural operators to steer age-grouped hunter-prey population models. The hard step is a scalar set by the Lotka-Sharpe integral rule, mapping birth and death rates to a single value. The team proved that map is Lipschitz, which means close neural stand-ins exist over compact rate sets. The resulting feedback law kept the system steady despite stand-in error, and tests showed online use under estimated rates.
arxiv-2604-04192: Adrienne Deganutti and team introduced GraphicDesignBench, the first comprehensive benchmark for AI on professional graphic design tasks. Unlike benchmarks focused on natural images or generic text-to-image work, it targets translating intent into structured layouts, faithful typographic text, layered compositions, valid vector graphics, and motion reasoning. The suite holds 50 tasks across five axes, layout, typography, infographics, template and design semantics, and animation, each tested for understanding and generation. Frontier closed-source models fell short on spatial judgment, faithful vector code, and fine type perception.
arxiv-2604-04292: Campbell, Del Debbio and Wallden introduce the circuit harmonic matrix, a table of Fourier terms over inputs and parameters. It shows how encoding, gates, start state and observable shape variance and the kernel, linking input shifts to sensitivity. It also limits what functions can be shown and lower-bounds error. For Clifford gates with Pauli or controlled rotations, a two-copy method computes covariance and the kernel in closed form. Across 400 setups, larger variance tracks faster learning and lower error for matching frequencies, showing bias toward lower frequencies.
arxiv-2604-04692: Jung, Yoon and Park challenge the belief that adding visual evidence always improves checking accuracy in fact-checking. Blanket use of visual evidence can reduce accuracy. The team proposes AMuFC, a modular fact-checking framework using two teamed vision-language models with distinct roles to enable adaptive use of visual evidence. Experiments on three sets, including new WebFC, show adaptive visual evidence use works well in fact-checking.
arxiv-2604-04892: Rege studies data attribution when models generate their own training data, as in online bandits, reinforcement learning, and language-model post-training. In such adaptive settings, one observation both updates the learner and shifts the data it will collect next. Standard attribution methods, built for fixed datasets, ignore that feedback loop. He formalizes occurrence-level attribution for finite-horizon adaptive learning through a conditional interventional target. He proves replay-side information cannot recover that target in general, and he identifies a structural class where logged data do identify it.
arxiv-2604-05192: Schmidt, Tanner, and Pinter speed up super splitting for phrase tokens. Byte Pair Coding caps tokens to full words, while BoundlessBPE and SuperBPE allow supers, mixes of chunks forming phrases. BoundlessBPE took 4.7 CPU days on 1GB of data. Merge hopefuls can be grouped by counts like regular chunks, avoiding full texts in memory. A plan splits regular merges from supers, and shows near-match with SuperBPE, whose knob becomes auto in the phase. Training on the 1GB takes 603 and 593 seconds for BoundlessBPE and SuperBPE, over 600 times faster.
arxiv-2604-05292: Blain and Noiseux present Broken by Default, a formal study of 3,500 code artifacts from seven language models across 500 security prompts. Each artifact is checked with the Z3 solver via COBALT, producing mathematical witnesses. Across models, 56 percent of artifacts contain at least one COBALT vulnerability; of these, 1,055 are formally proven via Z3 witnesses. GPT-4o leads at 62 percent, grade F, while Gemini 2.5 Flash is best at 48 percent, grade D, and no model earns better than D. Six industry tools combined miss 98 percent of Z3-proven findings.
arxiv-2604-05492: Llobera-Querol and ten colleagues ask whether black-hole merger remnants stay in their birth clusters or fly free, shaping later hierarchical mergers. From 84 events in the first half of run O4 plus 3 from the second, they compare field and cluster origins and compute recoil kicks. Five events favor dense-cluster birth, typical kicks reach a few hundred kilometers per second, and retention looks unlikely in globular clusters but possible in nuclear star clusters.
arxiv-2604-05892: King, Broadley, and Beneitez model elasto-inertial turbulence in cylinder arrays for thin polymer mixes. As stretch grows, wild flow sets in first through a subcritical saddle-node jump, then through gentler supercritical steps on a Ruelle-Takens-Newhouse path, fed by wake shedding and bulk flow. Wake-channel flow splits energy spectra in two, and arrowhead shapes fade as inertia rises.
arxiv-2604-05992: Richard, Khotyaintsev, and Norgren survey flat-top electron velocity distributions in fast magnetotail plasma jets with a new sorting method. Only about 7 percent of jet distributions are flat-topped, yet most jets show them, marking parallel acceleration and electron streaming as a jet hallmark. Flat-tops cluster in an ion-inertial-length-scale patch near current-sheet edges close to the reconnection zone.
arxiv-2604-06192: Gonzàlez and three colleagues explain when falling entropy during reasoning actually tracks correctness in language models. Their Stepwise Informativeness Assumption requires entropy-reducing reasoning steps to raise the probability of valid answers on average. Next-token prediction can move answer-relevant information from training data without guaranteeing that alignment, which instead depends on how training couples reasoning traces to correct answers. Tests across four benchmarks and varied open-weight models show entropy-correctness alignment grows with post-training but weakens when tasks exceed model capabilities.
arxiv-2604-06392: Bhardwaj presents Qualixar OS for universal AI agent orchestration. Against kernel-level AIOS or single-framework AutoGen and CrewAI, it runs multi-agent systems across 10 providers, 8 frameworks, and 7 transports. Features include 12 multi-agent topologies, Forge, three-layer model routing, a consensus judge pipeline, four-layer content attribution, and the Claw Bridge for MCP and A2A protocols. A dashboard adds a visual workflow builder and skill marketplace. Validation covers 2,821 test cases. On a custom 20-task suite, it hits 100 percent accuracy at 0.000039 dollars per task. Source is available under Elastic License.
arxiv-2604-06492: Lowy pins down the best achievable error rate for private stochastic convex optimization under heavy tails. Earlier work had settled the zero-concentrated privacy version, but the pure epsilon-differential-privacy case stayed open. Assuming only a bounded k-th moment instead of a worst-case Lipschitz cap, his method hits the optimal rate up to log factors in polynomial time with high probability. It also runs in fixed polynomial time for hinge, ReLU, and absolute-value losses on balls, ellipsoids, and polytopes, even when the Lipschitz cap is infinite.
arxiv-2604-06792: Raviprakash and three colleagues extend planetary habitability indices to Venus-like worlds. The Earth Similarity Index ranks planets from Earth-like to dissimilar, and the Mars Similarity Index covers extreme life, yet Venus's upper atmosphere may also host extreme life under special conditions. Their Venus Similarity Index averages radius, density, escape velocity, and surface temperature in Venus units, running from total dissimilarity to maximum similarity. Ancient Venus and Future Earth indices add time depth, comparing early Venus with ancient Earth and tracing possible futures for Earth-like planets.
arxiv-2604-07392: Fan, Zhang, and Han propose ERA, a clear framework for embodied choice that beats black-box imitation. The world is stored as structured semantic events in a readable form. Choices come from pulling similar past event-action pairs from a store of cases. Final moves blend those retrieved moves by weight, keeping choices physical and open to check. Drone tests show real-time, adaptive moves in changing settings with no retraining.
arxiv-2604-07492: Platonov and Prokhorenkova propose cluster attention for graph machine learning, widening receptive fields without losing graph-structure biases. Message-passing nets are limited by layer count, while global-attention graph transformers ignore topology and its inductive biases. Cluster attention splits nodes into communities with standard detection methods and lets each node attend to all nodes in each cluster. The method keeps large receptive fields plus strong structural biases. Adding cluster attention to message-passing nets or graph transformers much improves scores across many graph datasets, including real-world GraphLand benchmarks.
arxiv-2604-07692: Nnamdi and four colleagues offer Tree-of-Evidence, a search method framing clarity as discrete tuning. Current methods, such as focus or highlights, often fail to show choice-making for mixed modes like time-series and text. Tree-of-Evidence employs Evidence filters scoring coarse data groups, and uses beam search to find the compact evidence set copying the model's guess. Across six tasks, Tree-of-Evidence retains over 0.98 of full-model AUROC using five evidence units, with higher choice match and lower truth error.
arxiv-2604-08392: Digge and four colleagues demonstrate that poisoned training data can systematically wreck controllers built directly from data, with no model in hand. Their recursive attack feeds false state paths that shift the apparent dynamics just enough that any linear feedback controller built from them destabilizes the real system. The attacker needs no knowledge of the system or of the synthesis method, and simulations confirm the effect with clean and noisy data alike.
arxiv-2604-08492: Schumacher, Reichelt, and Strohmaier test how vector size affects the stability of node embeddings across repeated runs. Across five methods, including node2vec, GraphSAGE, and VERSE, and many sizes and datasets, size mattered greatly but not uniformly. Some methods steadied at larger sizes while others wobbled or declined. Most importantly, the most stable sizes were not always the best performing ones, complicating how practitioners should pick a dimension.
arxiv-2604-08792: Barnaby and three colleagues replace labeled cases with multiple choice queries for clearing up programs. High level code specs are unclear, and labeled guidance is error prone. Their system presents small sets of high level acts as choices, each answer option marking a cluster of similar possible programs via a Hoare triple. The setup supports formal thinking about query value and optimal query building. Their Socrates tool builds clear queries across four rule based and neural domains, finding wanted programs more dependably than older methods.
arxiv-2604-08992: Prabhu and four colleagues extend distance formulae for square-cell configurations, subgraphs of the square lattice whose inner faces are all four-cycles, beyond symmetric cases. Earlier work gave total and average distance for tidy groups such as hexagonal, trapezium, and bitrapezium cases. The new work covers uneven cases of varied structure, showing how uneven shapes change the growth and distribution of pairwise distance. The result is a single scheme that treats symmetric and uneven square-cell graphs as special cases, with fresh insight into bent shapes.
arxiv-2604-09192: Jenčová studies signalling in higher order quantum maps from an order-theoretic view, building on a combinatorial account of higher order types. Types are represented by boolean functions called type functions, each tied to a structure poset. She characterizes the lattice of regular subtypes by a monotonicity condition: it is closed under the one-way signalling product and generated by causally ordered types. Signalling relations can then be read from the poset through a rank parity condition, with normal forms from maximal chains.
arxiv-2604-09292: Burle and Udovenko study restricted syndrome decoding, where each error entry comes from a fixed small set. This problem underlies CROSS, a post-quantum signature scheme and a NIST Round 2 candidate. Solutions can be deduced from structured small-norm vectors in newly built codes, in Hamming and Euclidean metrics. That reduces the problem to code-based and lattice-based problems, widening the attack surface and giving new security insight.
arxiv-2604-09492: Sinhababu, Bharati, Ganguly, and Mitra propose dynamic ranked list cuts for reranking pipelines. Common ways to cut reranking cost include candidate sets or comparison graphs skipping repeat matches. For pointwise rankers, a candidate set usually means guessing a query-based cutoff from top-ranked document scores. The authors argue limiting this to existing documents is needless, instead making a pseudo-relevant document with a large language model as a pivot. Tests show made pivots reduce pointwise calls by up to 66 percent, with listwise speedups of nearly three times.
arxiv-2604-09792: Anantharaman and Monk show a spectral gap of nearly two ninths for typical hyperbolic surfaces drawn from the Weil-Petersson probability measure. This intermediate result leads toward their proof of the optimal spectral gap of nearly a quarter, building on the first part of this series. Much of the proof uses explicit inclusion-exclusion counting to rule out tangles at the precision of one over the genus.
arxiv-2604-10092: Cacchiò studies how steady non-zonal flows of finite size arise on a spinning sphere under the two-dimensional Euler equations. Limiting the space to tetrahedral symmetry yields a scalar reduction. He tests four nonlinear forms: polynomial, sine-Gordon, sinh-Gordon, and exponential Liouville. The split point comes from spectral methods. Whether the split is subcritical or supercritical turns on the parity of the form and mass balance, not on shape alone.
arxiv-2604-10592: Punch, Guha, and Roedig show circuit cutting leaks secrets through dull metadata. Cloud logs for billing and upkeep can betray a user's algorithm without touching quantum data. Cutting a big program into small parts adds depth and gate bloat tied to hardware shape. That bloat fingerprint names the algorithm family and locality near perfectly on 12,000 fragments. Even on unseen sizes, family calls hold above 0.98, so metadata alone betrays intent.
arxiv-2604-10692: Fan and Zhang present i-Tac, an inverse-design pipeline for 3D-printed tactile elastomers used in vision-based touch sensors. Different sensor designs need different transparency and hardness, but conventional design proceeds by trial and error. Inspired by the human dermis, i-Tac combines three resins in PolyJet printing and maps compositions to properties with response-surface models. Given targets, an optimization step finds workable composition regions and an operating window. Experiments confirm tuning in one iteration, cutting the usual iterative burden.
arxiv-2604-10892: Wang and three colleagues propose HECTOR, a human-centered coordination scheme for robotic fleets under ongoing temporal tasks, where direct control of each robot is hard. It has three layers: a bidirectional, multimodal protocol for human-fleet interaction; rolling task assignment to teams in a horizon; and dynamic team coordination as subtasks emerge during execution. Missions can be temporal formulas over actions, and the layered design supports human interaction at varied triggers, improving efficiency and cutting effort. Human-in-the-loop simulations over fleets test temporal tasks and uncertainties.
arxiv-2604-10992: Shui and six colleagues present ArtiCAD, a training-free multi-agent system, the first of its kind, generating editable, articulated design assemblies from text or images. Four agents handle design, generation, assembly, and review. A key insight is predicting assembly links during design rather than assembly, using a connector that states attachment points and joint settings plainly. Checks plus cross-stage rollback isolate and correct design and code errors. A growing experience store gathers design knowledge. Tests on three datasets validate the approach, which also supports design and physical prototyping.
arxiv-2604-11392: Reimann and Eidecker-Dunkel show that absence of thermalization is possible after a local quench, not just a global one. In integrable models, global quenches can violate the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis while a weaker version still holds, but here even that version fails, a strong violation. The analysis uses XX spin chains with open boundaries, where a single-spin impurity at the chain end or center is switched on or changed after equilibrium. Numerics find similar behavior in XXZ models for an end impurity, but not for a central one.
arxiv-2604-11592: del Teso and two colleagues build a game framework for the doubly nonlinear parabolic equation. A new mean value formula for the p-Laplacian stays robust when the gradient vanishes and does not depend on the p-Laplacian's sign. This formula yields a dynamic programming principle whose solutions converge to a viscosity solution for the boundary value problem. Solutions to the principle match value functions for a stochastic two-player zero-sum game built and studied here.
arxiv-2604-11892: Li and eighteen colleagues present direct evidence of ram-pressure stripping in a post-starburst galaxy at redshift 3.06, the earliest such detection to date. Using JWST and ALMA data on A2744-JF-z3, in a galaxy group, they find ongoing removal of cold gas and dust alongside an abrupt halt to star formation. Against simulations predicting rarer stripping at high redshift, the result shows stripping can operate beyond redshift 3 through stochastic, impulsive removal in a clumpy, filamentary medium. It extends environmental quenching deep into the galaxy-assembly epoch.
arxiv-2604-12092: Matheu, Baras, and Belta reformulate temporal behavior trees using ternary signal logic, adding a third truth value, Unknown, for trajectories that have neither fully satisfied nor violated a specification. This moves analysis beyond offline post hoc study and trace repair toward control synthesis. They propose mixed-integer linear encodings for partial logic and these trees over ternary logic, enabling correct-by-construction control for linear dynamical systems via mixed-integer optimisation. Solving optimal control problems demonstrates the framework's utility.
arxiv-2604-12192: Lorenzo De Gaspari and two colleagues model a bushfire racing through a narrow gully. Burnable fuel fills the valley floor, while bare rock walls hold almost nothing. Ignition switches on when temperature crosses a threshold, drawing on nearby hot areas. In a very narrow gully, the full model collapses to a simpler equation. That equation runs along the gully's curving axis. The proof uses tailored estimates and a reflection argument.
arxiv-2604-12492: Marcus L. Marcussen and 13 colleagues solve the mu Herculis system after nearly three hundred years. The bright nearby quadruple anchors asteroseismology, the study of star vibrations. Its brightest star shows solar-like oscillations. A joint fit of velocities and sky paths spans Hipparcos, Gaia DR3, and ground records. The 2023 periastron passage of the inner pair pins the orbits. Masses land with sub-percent precision. The system parallax reconciles and improves earlier values.
arxiv-2604-12892: Shivani P. Shah and 13 colleagues assay thorium in 47 metal-poor stars. Thorium scatter falls from six tenths of a dex at low metallicity to two tenths higher up. Thorium tracks europium and dysprosium closely, with average ratio near zero. Absolute spans run just over one dex, with observed spread two tenths and intrinsic spread one tenth at low metallicity. About 68 percent of events vary within one third, while 5 percent vary by over three, nearing 10. The tight yields challenge models to find a prompt site.
arxiv-2604-12992: Alinezhad, Cao, Young, and Post build a diffusion model that predicts the full range of outcomes that might have happened for patients whose treatments change over time. Their Causal Diffusion Model handles shifting patient states and tangled, time-varying confounding with no separate deconfounding step. On a tumor-growth simulator, it beat leading causal methods for over-time data by 15 to 30 percent on outcome-range accuracy.
arxiv-2604-13092: Harikumar presents PlanCompiler, a compilation architecture for multi-step language-model workflows that splits planning from execution. The system writes a typed JSON plan over a fixed list of primitives, checks it against structural and type constraints, and turns only validated plans into executable Python. On a 300-task benchmark it wins 278 tasks overall, against 202 and 187 for free-form baselines, at $0.356 in planning cost versus $2.140 and $18.391.
arxiv-2604-13392: Yi and six colleagues build ReSS, a system that teaches language models to reason faithfully over tables in high-stakes fields like health care and finance. Symbolic models give checkable logic but lack rich meaning, while general models need special tuning for tables. ReSS uses a decision tree to pull out decision paths as symbolic scaffolds, then guides a language model to write reasoning that sticks to that logic. Fine-tuning on the resulting data, plus scaffold-invariant augmentation, lifts results over trees and standard tuning by up to 10 percent.
arxiv-2604-13592: Wang and eight colleagues give language models explicit foresight for play with other agents. In such games, each side must guess what the other will do next. Their method, Foresight Policy Optimization, builds opponent modeling into policy training. It weighs self-interest alongside the rival's likely moves. Two testbeds, Cooperative RSA and Competitive Taboo, support self-play trials. Trained models improve across sizes and origins, and they also do well in new settings they have not seen.
arxiv-2604-14092: Shi and colleagues compare spirals paired with ellipticals against spirals paired with spirals, using MaNGA spectra. Elliptical partners show suppressed central star formation and higher metal content, the reverse of spiral-spiral pairs. Both effects grow with the elliptical companion's mass. Lopsided gas flows boost star formation within elliptical pairs. The pattern fits suppressed gas inflow inside the companion's hot halo, with close encounters squeezing gas and sparking new metals.
arxiv-2604-14292: Russell and five colleagues observe the Ophiuchus cluster with XRISM Resolve, tracking motion behind its largest radio bubble. They detect a shift near minus 80 kilometers per second into the wake, with dispersion rising from about 135 to about 210. The shift and rise concentrate at the wake center, matching the splash under a rising bubble. In the cool core, turbulent energy is only 1 percent of thermal energy radiated over 7 billion years. Turbulent heating reaches only a third of cooling luminosity, so wake motions cannot stop cooling.
arxiv-2604-14692: Wu and eight colleagues built Chain-of-Glimpse, a video-reasoning method that ties each reasoning step to a specific visible object region instead of leaning on overall saliency. A search-guided controller, trained with reinforcement learning that rewards well-grounded answers, builds these traces step by step into interpretable multi-step decisions. Tests on NExTQA, Video-Holmes, CG-Bench Reasoning, and VRBench showed steady gains and stronger generalization across varied video tasks.
arxiv-2604-15292: Nortmann and 15 colleagues hunt for atmospheric gases on the sub-Neptune GJ 1214 b using eight transits from the CRIRES+ spectrograph. Five candidate molecules go undetected, with upper limits set by injection tests, while carbon dioxide shows a tentative signal with signal-to-noise near 3.6. A retrieval analysis favors a metal-rich atmosphere, consistent with earlier JWST hints, though more data are needed to confirm the detection.
arxiv-2604-15392: An and three colleagues speed up physics-informed neural networks, which often train slowly and shakily on hard partial differential equations. Their light curvature-aware scheme adds an adaptive fix to standard first-order optimizers, using back-to-back gradient gaps as a cheap gauge of changing loss shape. Tests across PDE benchmarks show faster convergence, steadier training, and better accuracy, including on high-dimensional heat flow.
arxiv-2604-15592: Seydi and Miabey study A-coherent and A-quasi-coherent sheaves over ringed spaces in algebraic geometry over non-algebraically closed fields. An O_X-module counts as A-coherent when it admits a global presentation by finite-rank free modules, and A-quasi-coherent for arbitrary rank. Under flatness and exactness conditions, these sheaves match finitely presented modules over global sections, yielding faithful flatness for Nash-to-analytic homomorphisms.
arxiv-2604-15692: Nakamura, Kotorii, and Leonov map how flow drives skyrmioniums, donut-like spin knots with no net twist charge, in chiral magnets. Even with zero net charge, the knots veer sideways, since inner knot and outer ring cover unlike areas, and warped shapes widen the gap, giving Hall bends like skyrmions. At high flow, knots stretch, fold into skyrmions, melt into drops, or spread into stripes, by field and pull. Knot-skyrmion grids show springy hauls, shape swaps, soliton trades, and stripe growth, and pulses open more regimes.
arxiv-2604-15992: Pablo F. Castro introduces SATFuL, a SAT solver for fuzzy logics, built on mixed-integer non-linear programming solvers. Boolean SAT solvers abound, but fuzzy SAT has drawn less attention despite useful applications. Unlike other fuzzy solvers, SATFuL handles all major versions of fuzzy propositional logic, while rivals target specific versions. Tests show performance comparable to leading fuzzy solvers for Lukasiewicz logic, and better than available solvers for Product logic. The approach is sound and complete, and extends easily to new fuzzy operators.
arxiv-2604-16692: Thériault and colleagues reveal full molecule tilt spreads in organic thin films via light tests. Device work depends on tilt, yet standard tools reveal only the first two moments. Diverse spreads can share low-order means while varying in function, hiding true layout. Multi-tone nonlinear light tests with the Maximum Entropy Method reconstruct the distribution without prior assumptions. The method resolves asymmetry and bimodality invisible to probes, benchmarking dynamics simulations. Simulations often miss the complex distribution despite predicting the first two moments, making tilt an observable.
arxiv-2604-16792: Williams and colleagues study how clusters shape halo assembly in quiescent galaxies. Stellar haloes, built by hierarchical accretion, preserve signatures of galaxy growth. Samples span redshift zero point one to one point zero, with cluster and field quiescent galaxies. Cluster galaxies build haloes faster, with about 23 percent larger growth at low mass and about 40 percent at high mass. High-mass cluster galaxies host more luminous haloes, while low-mass ones host less luminous ones. Higher-mass cluster galaxies grow haloes through mergers, while lower-mass ones lose outer material.
arxiv-2604-17292: Boucetta gives a complete description of flat Lorentzian Lie groups, settling a long-standing open problem in pseudo-Riemannian geometry. The main result splits all such groups into two kinds: those carrying a timelike parallel left-invariant vector field, and those of Kundt type, with six explicit classes for the underlying algebra. A refined study of the double extension process reveals that all these algebras arise, directly or in a generalized sense, from flat Euclidean ones. Full classifications in dimensions three and four follow, unifying several earlier partial results.
arxiv-2604-17392: Drogosz and Łygan test Fermi-Dirac statistics, rather than its simpler Boltzmann approximation, in simulations of perfect spin hydrodynamics for spin-half particles. Their system is boost-invariant and transversely uniform, with spin corrections entering the baryon current and energy-momentum tensor at second order. The special functions in the Fermi-Dirac coefficients prove easy to parametrize, making the approach feasible. For earlier initial conditions, differences between the two statistics run about ten times smaller than spin-feedback corrections, though solutions can break down at very large spin polarization.
arxiv-2604-17492: Kouzelis, Gidaris, and Komodakis rethink how diffusion models for images use high-level cues. Older work pairs image latents with cues from a fixed, pre-trained encoder. Their CoReDi method lets that cue space shift during training through a small learned linear projection. Stop-gradient targets, normalization, and extra rules keep the shifting space from caving in. Used for both latent and pixel-space image work, the method sharpens how cues match raw image data.
arxiv-2604-17592: Caldwell, Spencer, Kissinger, and Rand build TensorRocq, tools for diagram reasoning in Rocq. Symmetric monoidal categories frame computing as steps put side by side and in sequence. String diagrams reason about their equations by showing links. Yet in Rocq, rigid equation structure hides those links behind symbol shuffling. TensorRocq converts between symbol-based terms and hypergraphs with interfaces while keeping a common tensor meaning. It spots when terms match and rewrites up to diagram deformation. Users can build simple theories from generators and relations and work with equations within them.
arxiv-2604-17692: Xue and thirteen colleagues introduce AccelCIM, a dataflow exploration tool for SRAM compute-in-memory accelerators. SRAM compute-in-memory offers high density and energy efficiency for deep networks, but limited room creates on/off-chip traffic cost for large models. Prior studies assume models fit fully on-chip, leaving design untapped. AccelCIM maps a design space of CIM macro setups and macro-array layouts, and tests designs with cycle-accurate sim and PPA checks. Broad testing on typical LLM workloads yields useful insights for sound CIM design.
arxiv-2604-17892: Yuyan Zhou and six colleagues inject controllable randomness into latent reasoning for large language models, using Gumbel-Softmax sampling to restore diverse reasoning paths that deterministic latent methods lose. Their LEPO framework then applies reinforcement learning directly to continuous latent representations, keeping sampling stochastic during rollouts while building one unified gradient estimate for latent states and discrete tokens during optimization. Tests show it beats existing reinforcement methods for both discrete and latent reasoning.
arxiv-2604-17992: Huang and Wang investigate one-dimensional trivial magnetic solitons in ferromagnetic nanowires, studied in theory and in simulation. An approximate math model using two free parameters matches computer runs. Across an interface between media of unlike anisotropy, soliton reflection and refraction act very oddly, unlike linear spin waves. Switching field or spin current pulses in reverse across nearby regions make pairs of them moving apart, each set by how they are made. They can drive domain wall motion over lengths set by soliton size, suiting digital spintronics.
arxiv-2604-18092: Podstawski investigates generalization of tuned small language models in graph inference. The study tests two axes: graph size and graph family distribution. With three instruction tuned models of 3 to 4 billion parameters and two serialization formats, it tests graphs much larger than the training range. It also tests held out random graph families. Tuned models keep strong ordinal consistency across distinct families. They keep ranking graphs by structure on larger inputs, with varying degradation by architecture. The findings map reliable generalization zones for graph reasoning tasks.
arxiv-2604-18192: Nurkanović analyzes sequential quadratic programming for optimization problems with complementarity constraints. Such problems break standard constraint qualifications at every feasible point, making them very hard to solve in practice. His main result gives local convergence of the SQPCC method to S-stationary points under weaker second-order conditions, with no strict complementarity needed. He also proves that the active sets settle after a finite number of steps in some cases, and he tests the theory with numeric examples.
arxiv-2604-18592: Hůla and four colleagues offer a 2D early exit method joining layer and sentence exits. Handling input sentence-by-sentence while switching on deeper layers gives stacked savings over either side. Four LLMs on three sentiment sets show speed-ups of about one and a half to two times over layer-wise exit. Fine-tuning reduces but keeps this edge. The approach is model-neutral, needs only lightweight plugs, and pairs with quantization. 2D early exit excels when meaning builds smoothly, hinting at sequence tasks beyond sentiment work.
arxiv-2604-18992: Jiang and Huang model how unresolved compact binaries build the galactic wave foreground. Only a few shine brightly enough to resolve alone, while the rest merge into a confusion haze. They treat it as an anisotropic background and derive how detector response varies with source positions. They also test whether resolved systems fairly mirror the whole population. Within the Taiji Data Challenge II, estimates built from resolved binaries prove early viable.
arxiv-2604-19192: Radež and Bohak enhance NPCs with language models and computer vision for awareness of place. Standard characters use pre-scripted dialogue and lack spatial understanding. Their method captures wide images, applies segmentation to find objects and positions, and builds a JSON picture from locations plus scene graph data as directional vectors. The picture feeds the model, letting characters name nearby objects and landmarks. An expert interview refined the system, and a user study found players liked aware characters over a baseline.
arxiv-2604-19292: Mor-Lan and colleagues probe hidden locale biases in multilingual language models with LocQA, a set of 2,156 questions in 12 languages about locale-dependent facts like laws, dates, and measures. The questions name no locale except through the asking language, so answers reveal each model's implicit defaults. Testing 32 models uncovers two structural bias types. Across languages, models lean toward answers fitting the United States locale, even when the question language points elsewhere.
arxiv-2604-19392: Zhuang, Dos Santos, and Han propose HarmoniDiff-RS, a training-free diffusion method for blending composite satellite images across diverse domains. Satellite image blending matters for remote sensing tasks like data augmentation, disaster simulation, and urban planning. Their method aligns source and target domains with a latent mean shift that moves radiometric traits between them. A timestep-wise latent fusion balances blending with content preservation, and a light harmony classifier picks the most coherent result.
arxiv-2604-19592: Farina and Perdomo give a black-box reduction from online learning to online multicalibration, in the style of Gordon, Greenwald, and Marks. To achieve high-dimensional multicalibration for a class of functions, it suffices to combine any no-regret learner over that class with an expected variational inequality solver. They also prove the converse: efficient multicalibration implies efficient solver performance. That converse shows how expected variational inequalities mirror the role of fixed points in the Gordon-Greenwald-Marks result for phi-regret.
arxiv-2604-19992: Klos and Piatti model the age gap among Large Magellanic Cloud star clusters, the scarcity of clusters aged four to eleven billion years. They link star formation to cluster masses with a power-law maximum-mass rule, at 5 percent forming efficiency. Mass loss from N-body simulations plus a completeness limit yields the observable fraction. Their model reproduces the gap when peak masses stay low, but needs peaks of at least two hundred thousand solar masses for ancient globulars. The gap thus reflects history and detection limits.
arxiv-2604-20192: Deng, Fu, Li, and Wu study dynamic multi battle contests and how contest shape drives incentives and rent dissipation. A discouragement effect, seen in tug-of-war bouts and best-of-K games, often blocks full dissipation even in endless series. They pin down exchangeability as a structural trait feeding the effect, with a complete if-and-only-if rule for almost full dissipation. As a test case, the iterated incumbency contest shows how swings in the environment keep incentives alive and yield almost full dissipation.
arxiv-2604-20292: Homma, Katsuragawa, and Matsuzaki show fifth force suppression can come from symmetry alone, without screening. Their mirror Standard Model extension, symmetric under a twofold flip, breaks scale invariance, yielding a scalaron as a pseudo Nambu Goldstone boson. The scalaron couples to the trace anomaly gap between Standard Model and mirror sectors, tying fifth force strength to scalaron mass with no free knobs. The Standard Model then predicts strength near a thousandth above ten centimetres for scalaron mass near a millionth of an electronvolt, in reach of next tests.
arxiv-2604-20392: Prisadnikov and three colleagues build a self taught pretraining scheme for an iterative vision Transformer for any image size. Standard Transformers scale poorly with image size, leaving DINO stuck at low detail. A foveal inspired model instead handles fixed size multi zoom patches in sequence, without backpropagation through time. Their sequential to global self taught frame, built on DINO self distillation, pretrains size agnostic encoders at scale. ImageNet 1K and downstream tasks match rivals while compute stays flat at any input size.
arxiv-2604-20492: Bermudez, Perlaza, and Esnaola show that scattered learners can match a central learner without pooling raw data. Each client trains with empirical risk minimization plus relative-entropy regularization, a penalty that keeps its model near a reference. It passes only its Gibbs measure, a probability weighting over models, to the next client. That chain lets each step inherit the prior client inductive bias, with regularization scaled to local sample sizes. The decentralized result then equals the central one, shifting collaboration from sharing data to sharing bias.
arxiv-2604-20992: Yu presents a short guide to second-order optimality conditions for MPECs, mathematical programs with equilibrium constraints. He starts from the classical nonlinear programming template and explains why it breaks down for such programs. He then develops three viewpoints from the wider field: multiplier-based tests, implicit-programming tests built on the lower-level solution map, and piecewise tests that split complementarity structure into smooth pieces. Critical cones, strong regularity, and curvature's exact role take center stage here.
arxiv-2604-21092: Gricel Vázquez and four colleagues build COMPASS, a system that writes explanations for automated task plans and adjusts its own prompts as users react. It models hidden mental states like attention and understanding as a decision problem, letting its policy adapt wording and detail to each person. Tested on two cyber-physical cases, the method shows that folding user feedback into prompt design can make opaque planning steps legible.
arxiv-2604-22092: Shakeri and three colleagues present FlashSpread, a GPU framework fusing the renewal pipeline for non-Markovian epidemic simulation into one Triton kernel. Intermediates never leave registers, and skips preserve CUDA Graph capture, while degree-aware dispatch keeps top speed on scale-free graphs. On one NVIDIA A100, the fused engine hits 8.09 Giga-NUPS at N = 10^6, a 217x speedup over optimized CPU tau-leaping. On a Barabasi-Albert graph, merge dispatch recovers more than 4x, from under half to 2 Giga-NUPS, and the framework reaches N = 10^8 on one A100.
arxiv-2604-22192: Zheng and eight colleagues present CharTide, redesigning training and alignment data for chart-to-code generation. First, Tri-Perspective Tuning splits training into sight, pure-text code logic, and modality fusion, letting a 7B model beat baselines on supervised data. Second, alignment becomes data verification, not heuristic scoring, through Inquiry-Driven RL: downstream models should answer identical visual queries the same for original and generated charts. A frozen Inspector verifies generated charts through atomic QA. On ChartMimic, Plot2Code, and ChartX, CharTide-7B/8B beats open-source rivals.
arxiv-2604-22492: Chen and Chen explore whether multimodal large language models can analyse raw video of mice and predict dominance hierarchy. They introduce MTT-Bench, a benchmark of annotated pairwise mouse interaction videos for Mouse Tube Test work. Building on existing architectures, they fine-tune models for zero-shot inference on unseen clips, predicting dominance without labels during testing. Their framework shows high agreement with tube test rankings. The work opens a new direction for using foundation models for ethology and social behaviour analysis, without special models.
arxiv-2604-22892: Yermekov and Herrera-Martí extend their dual-criterion feature selection with reinforcement learning in StackFeat-RL, which tunes the method's settings by policy gradients. The dual rule demands both coefficient consistency and selection frequency, guarding against failure modes that single-rule methods miss, while repeated rounds give convergence guarantees. On COVID-19 miRNA data and three Alzheimer's classification tasks, it reaches the highest predictive accuracy among the methods tested. It does so using three to four times fewer features than its rivals.
arxiv-2604-23192: Aditya and three colleagues study how conservation laws shape quantum coherence spread in many-body dynamics. Across U(1) random circuits, charge-dipole circuits, and ergodic Hamiltonian dynamics, they probe coherence globally and locally. Global probes use participation entropy; local probes use relative entropy of coherence. Conservation laws replace log saturation in unconstrained circuits with slow hydrodynamic easing of global coherence. Locally, symmetry-bound circuits show a rise-peak-fall pattern whose peak time grows as a power of subsystem size. Ergodic Hamiltonians stretch the peak into a long plateau.
arxiv-2604-23592: Jahan, Sadeghnezhad, and Ziaie study spherical collapse of an inhomogeneous fluid in Rastall gravity, a theory that tweaks how matter couples to spacetime curvature. By tuning the theory's parameter so the effective radial pressure vanishes, they obtain exact solutions in which collapsing shells bounce instead of forming a singularity. Trapped surfaces can also be avoided, so the bounce is not hidden behind a horizon, and the weak energy condition holds.
arxiv-2604-23692: Chu and colleagues build a streaming system for personalised audio-driven facial animation that needs no look-ahead and no scripted calibration recording. A causal motion tokenizer captures both broad timing and fine articulatory detail, while a style retriever draws on arbitrary casual clips of the target person. The result beats prior methods on lip-sync, identity consistency, and realism while preserving real-time telepresence constraints.
arxiv-2604-23792: Zhou, Malz, Schafer, Malanchev, Cabrera-Vives, and Hernández improve sky-survey light-curve classification by using classifiers' past scores rather than only their final labels. Using synthetic LSST data, they combine a recurrent net plus an attention module. This lifts accuracy and evens out precision and recall over existing challenge classifiers. They also propose new metrics based on the Wasserstein distance between shifting prediction patterns. These metrics capture stable scores, accuracy, and early performance on limited data.
arxiv-2604-23892: Zaeed, Islam, and Indic present Optimas, a modular AI framework that turns speed reports into code fixes automatically. It maps reports to proven code changes, joining insight extraction, code generation, execution, and validation in one pipeline. Across 3,410 real-world experiments it generates fully correct code and improves performance in nearly all cases, with average gains from about 8 percent to about 79 percent on NVIDIA GPUs.
arxiv-2604-23992: Verdugo and four colleagues rebuild the cosmic expansion history with a generalized deceleration curve. It adds an early radiation-like term to a late-time component. Fitted to chronometers, supernovae, galaxy, and quasar data, the model still finds the universe accelerating today. Its switch from slowing to speeding comes earlier than the standard model expects, with slightly weaker late acceleration.
arxiv-2604-24292: Romero and three colleagues offer a regularization method for divergent integrals in quantum field theory. The method splits the integrand's expansion into singular parts and finite parts. It then subtracts only the singular sector while keeping symmetry. In single-scale theories, renormalized values gain a log pattern fixed by the ultraviolet tail alone, apart from standard renormalization-group flows. The method needs only tail structure, and also fits theories with modified dispersion and infrared singularities.
arxiv-2604-24492: Thind and three colleagues build low-precision training into the search for neural network shapes meant for small space hardware, instead of shrinking precision only after the search ends. That late shrink step had left a gap between how a design behaved while being searched and how it ran on board. Tested on ship spotting from orbit with a small vision chip, their aligned training kept accuracy close to full precision, reaching 0.826 on the same scale without adding model size.
arxiv-2604-24592: Barbieri and Di Cintio develop a method for the steady states of a system with no collisions. It is held by an outside force and fed at its edges by fixed rules for putting particles back. They widen the usual flux-weighted Maxwellian edge scheme with an integer parameter. From Liouville's theorem they get an explicit formula for the steady distribution. Only the usual scheme gives thermal equilibrium. Other cases give non-thermal profiles, with uneven density and temperature gradients caused by the edges alone.
arxiv-2604-24792: Wani, Abdi, Naik and Al-Kuwari study quantum gravimetry with uncertain interrogation time. The uncertainty comes from a fundamental limit tied to energy-time relations. For linearly coupled gravimeters, they profile time from the two-parameter Fisher matrix. The time block is quadratic in the gravity parameter. The cross term becomes affine in g for quadratic background dynamics. This yields a formula for the gravity information retained when time is a nuisance parameter. Three benchmark models give conditions for minimizing time-information loss.
arxiv-2604-24892: Veenema and colleagues study the inner region of NGC 7582, a nearby Seyfert 2 galaxy. It hosts a star-forming disk and an AGN-driven outflow shaped like two cones. Using JWST spectroscopy, they analyse ionic lines spanning about 8 to 126 electronvolts. Low-ionisation lines trace ordered disk rotation, while high-ionisation lines follow the outflow. Outflow gas shows higher velocity spread than disk gas, at 119 versus 78 kilometres per second. The outflow can push gas beyond escape velocity, so most gas is unlikely to return.
arxiv-2604-25392: Mayzaroh and three colleagues rate PyCaret AutoML next to IndoBERT tuning for binary sentiment analysis of Indonesian Twitter notes on Ibu Kota Nusantara, or IKN. The set holds 1,472 samples: 780 negative and 692 positive. Logistic Regression, Naive Bayes, and Support Vector Machine were tried with 10-fold cross-checks, with Logistic Regression best. The indobert-base-p1 model was tuned for five epochs, hitting 89.59 percent accuracy. IndoBERT beats the plain machine learning baselines by far, showing the worth of Transformer-based reads for casual Indonesian social media text.
arxiv-2604-25692: Jordaan and Kumar complete the zero-interlacing picture for polynomial pairs that miss interlacing by two points. They use mixed recurrence relations to locate the pair of missing points. Then they prove the completion works for polynomials with real zeros in general. The same completion yields Wronskian-type bounds for the original pairs. Jacobi, Meixner-Pollaczek, and Pseudo-Jacobi families all get the treatment. For the doubly shifted Jacobi pair, the authors name the two points outright and sharpen prior results.
arxiv-2604-25892: Andrenšek studies dynamics and shape in Kiselman's semigroup. He introduces a level function, described simply through right multiplication by generators. Every sequence of partial products in the semigroup eventually stops changing. For random partial products, with each generator picked with positive chance, the wait until the final constant value is a sum of n independent geometric variables. A natural ultrametric built from the level function yields basic facts about metric balls and spheres.
arxiv-2604-25992: Taylor, Das Sarma, and Musser chart a route to an electronic quantum charge liquid, a state of fermions at fractional filling that keeps translation intact. Spinless fermions at filling 3/2 pair into bosons at 3/4 filling per unit cell. A square-lattice tetramer model generalizes the dimer model as a bosonic candidate at that filling. Its models show a local Z4 symmetry. Numerics find one tetramer wavefunction gapless from U(1)^3 symmetry, another definitively gapped. That gapped state is proposed as a bosonic charge liquid with minimal Z4 topological order.
arxiv-2604-26192: Gomes and four colleagues review how large language models assist empirical software engineering. They gather fifty peer-reviewed studies from 2020-2025 across twelve leading venues. They catalog sixty-nine aided tasks, mostly in mining software repos and lab tests on sorting, sifting, and grading. Use stays largely auto-led, not choice-aiding, with speed and scale gains set against hallucinations, uneven results, prompt effects, and gaps in rerun reporting. The paper closes with a research agenda for more sound use.
arxiv-2604-26492: Enttsel and Corlay proposed adaptive transform coding for squeezing semantic features, the compact vectors images are reduced to for machine inference. The idea follows the conditional rate-distortion rule for a Gaussian mixture: the coder picks transforms and quantizers by the inferred source mode. That freedom handles varied feature spreads better than one fixed coder. Tests on vision backbones and foundation models matched or beat leading neural compression methods while staying easy to interpret.
arxiv-2604-26692: Sutcliffe and Mutyamsetty propose a hybrid quantum approach to malware containment, framed as limiting likely spread while balancing the cost of cutting network links. Classical methods lean on Monte Carlo runs and greedy edge removal, both costly in compute. Quantum amplitude estimation replaces Monte Carlo sampling, cutting the cost of guessing from squared to linear in the inverse error, while Grover minimum finding cuts needed checks to square-root scaling. Classical runs and small hardware tests support the expected scaling, though large-scale use awaits error-proof devices.
arxiv-2604-26792: Godwood and four colleagues compare qudit and qubit encodings for fault-tolerant quantum simulation of lattice field theories. They price the non-Clifford gates needed for quadratic diagonal evolutions, using either one multi-level qudit or the equivalent binary qubits. For product-formula simulation, qudits would need an exponentially stronger synthesis edge to win outright, and for block-encoded methods qubits grow cheaper as dimension rises. Still, at small dimensions qudits can save a constant factor, mainly in block-encoded designs.
arxiv-2604-27192: Gadelrab and Reimann-Zitz use lattice Boltzmann simulations in a lubrication-theory framework to map how thin liquid films dewet, or pull apart into drops. Film thickness, surface energy, wettability, and intermolecular forces set the kinetics and long-time shape, which matter for coating quality. Master curves for the time to dewet show a strong power-law sensitivity to thickness and only weak sensitivity to moderate contact-angle changes. After rupture, coverage settles at a plateau that hints at a window for stabilization.
arxiv-2604-27292: McCann separates governance of effects from governance of model outputs. Effects mean actions like API calls, database writes, and tool invocations, not output concerns like content quality and bias. Any system performing effects is bounded twice: by what it can do, and by what governance covers. Yet in nearly all deployed AI systems those boundaries are set independently. Independence creates three regions, and two of them are failure modes. Governed capabilities, the only useful region, face ungoverned capabilities, a risk, and policies aimed at capabilities that do not exist, theater.
arxiv-2604-27592: Saini and Singh study polynomial maps with constants on matrix algebras for a simple two-term form. With one coefficient invertible, they relate the map's surjectivity to the nullity of the other coefficient. For two-by-two matrices, the images were already fully settled in earlier work. For three- and four-by-four matrices, they classify surjectivity through necessary and sufficient conditions on size, power, and nullity.
arxiv-2604-27692: Kai Gao, Yu Sun, and Chang-ai Sun present the first comprehensive study of bugs in template engine-based applications. Studying 1,004 bugs over 15 template engines and five programming languages, they identify symptoms, root causes, and common fix patterns. Abnormal rendering, such as unexpected or blank output, is the most common symptom at 48.61 percent, often appearing as silent failures. The 17 root causes are led by incompatible integration, syntax misuse, and mismatched data context. About 68 percent of bugs are fixed in the template, and over 20 percent need host-side logic changes.
arxiv-2605-00092:
A large team from the LISA Astrophysics Working Group compares forecasts for mergers of massive black holes, the kind the future LISA space observatory hopes to hear. When two galaxies merge, their central black holes should sink together and join. How often that happens depends on how the black holes form, feed, and move.

The project gathers about twenty published models and simulations, each with its own view of black hole and galaxy physics. It also adds the delays that occur while a pair slowly hardens before joining. By lining the forecasts up side by side, the team maps the spread in expected LISA event rates. That spread shows which model choices matter most for planning the mission's science.
arxiv-2605-00292:
Bingzheng Gan and 6 co-authors introduce Caracal, a language model architecture that replaces attention with Fourier mixing. Attention grows costly very fast as sequences lengthen, and position codes add their own limits. Caracal instead mixes information across a sequence with the Fast Fourier Transform, a classic signal processing tool, at a much gentler cost growth.

A frequency-domain masking trick, built from uneven padding and trimming, keeps the model causal so it can generate text step by step. Unlike some rival efficient designs, Caracal uses only standard library operations, which makes it portable across hardware. In evaluations it performed competitively against Transformer and state-space baselines. The authors present it as a simple, scalable path for modeling long sequences.
arxiv-2605-00592:
Martin C. Cooper and Imane Bousdira give a new meaning to fairness for machine learning classifiers when features constrain each other. The accepted idea, that a decision should not depend on protected traits such as gender, can be gamed by constraints linking the inputs, which hide the dependency. Their rule: call a decision fair when it has a fair explanation, the smallest reason for the outcome that mentions no protected trait, with constraints counted when judging smallness.

Oddly, ignoring constraints can flip a decision's fairness fully, even when no constraint links protected and plain traits at all. The authors then compare three meanings of a fair classifier: every call has only fair reasons, every call has a fair reason, or flipping protected traits never changes outcomes. They map how the three relate and study how costly it is to test each one.
arxiv-2605-00892:
Chamani Shiranthika and one co-author compare two ways to handle domain differences in federated medical imaging, where hospitals train together without sharing raw data. Model-side tuning adapts settings for each client, while data-side alignment reduces spread in the inputs. Despite wide use, the two strategies had not been compared head to head under one framework.

Across six settings of both task kinds, a conditional trade-off emerges. Alignment works better when gaps are mainly in appearance, as in chest X-ray sorting. Tuning works better when gaps are structural, as in colon polyp work. When spread is small, both do similarly. The authors give practical guidelines and point toward hybrid methods.
arxiv-2605-01092:
Pablo Rocha studies fractional type operators on Hardy spaces built over ball quasi-Banach function spaces, a broad family that covers many concrete function spaces. The operators are generated by orthogonal matrices with a fractional parameter and a multiplicity parameter. Rocha proves bounded extensions of the operators between the associated Hardy space and suitable target spaces, treating both the genuinely fractional case and the endpoint case separately.

In particular, the results apply to weighted Lebesgue, variable Lebesgue, Lorentz, and Orlicz spaces, with the last two described as new. Proofs rely on rotational invariance of the underlying space. They also use weighted Hardy space theory, a Rubio de Francia iteration algorithm, and finite atomic decomposition of the Hardy space. That gives a unified treatment across the family.
arxiv-2605-01392:
Yifei Wang and seven co-authors report how software developers actually use large language models while designing software, a stage long seen as pure human judgment. Hard facts on this use have been scarce, so the team mixes two sources of proof.

First, they mine 291 developer chats with ChatGPT that were shared on GitHub. From these they sort nine kinds of design task, from system architecture to data models and design patterns. They find most use is knowledge lookup and design-related code drafting at the detail level. Second, they survey 65 working developers. Those developers name seven gains, such as better tech choices and early flaw spotting, and six limits, such as long outputs, broken code, and weak grasp of project context. Together the two views ground a factual picture of current practice.
arxiv-2605-01592:
Satyabrata Jana, Debabrata Pal, Bodhayan Roy, and Sasanka Roy study the Witness Set problem, a dual of the classic art gallery question. A witness set is a set of points such that each spot in the polygon can be seen by at most one of them. The task is to tell whether a witness set of target size exists.

For simple polygons the team prove the problem sits in both NP and the parameterized class XP, a sharp contrast with the gallery problem, recently shown complete for a much harder class. Their route is combinatorial: a discretization sized by the target count yields a matching algorithm. An old claim of hardness was never backed by a proof. They show only the discrete variant is NP-complete, for rectilinear polygons with holes, where points must come from a given finite set. Hardness of the main problem stays open.
arxiv-2605-01792:
Shulamit Edelstein and seven co-authors compute with a vibrating sliver of light and matter. An optomechanical oscillator, a cavity whose mirror moves, crosses a Hopf threshold between two lives. Below it sits a still point jittered by thermal Brownian motion, with linear response and almost no memory. Above it, a self-sustained ringing is fed by radiation pressure and companion effects.

That ringing state works as a reservoir computer. Tapping the phonon-lasing cycle perturbs it, and the device answers with nonlinear transformations while holding short-term memory, no external feedback loop required. One chip-scale device with twenty virtual nodes rebuilds nonlinear functions, forecasts chaotic series, and classifies spoken digits on a two-digit task. Its mechanical tone sets the processing clock, near half a gigahertz in this build. The family of such devices reaches far higher, a path the authors draw toward ultrafast integrated physical computing.
arxiv-2605-01892:
George Fatouros and colleagues argue that banks and other financial firms need a different kind of security platform.
