Security teams often have plenty of alerts, but too little capacity to reason through them, and many breaches follow alerts that were never checked. The authors propose CyberAId, a system to be run on site and built from cooperating language model agents.

In the design, specialist agents work over normal security telemetry rather than replacing it, share state across firms without sharing private data, and map findings to the rules each firm must meet. Human control stays bounded and explicit. The team plans tests on fraud, money laundering, bank incident response, and trading resilience.
arxiv-2605-01992:
Milad Solbi, Daris Samart, and Peera Simakachorn revisit inflation models that recent sky data have put under pressure. Data from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope favour a higher spectral index than before, which strains alpha-attractor T-models and natural inflation. The authors place those models inside K-inflation, where the field's kinetic term depends on the field itself and adds friction.

That extra friction shifts both models into the regions favoured by combined Planck, ACT, and other data. The analysis also refines the reheating term and checks the models against Swampland ideas about valid gravity theories. For the T-model case studied, viable values predict matter-like reheating and a gravitational wave background unlikely to be seen soon.
arxiv-2605-02092:
Bing Zhou and colleagues present NORA, an autonomous research agent built for spatial data science and GIScience. General research agents lack the specialised reasoning, method choice, and data access that rigorous spatial work needs. NORA runs the full research cycle through a skills-first design with twenty-one domain workflow skills and nine specialist sub-agents, linked by custom protocol servers.

Two skills stand out. A spatial analysis skill encodes decision frames for exploratory analysis, spatial regression, and diagnostics. A spatial download skill gathers data from authoritative sources in a reproducible way. The system is presented as a harness-engineered agent, where the surrounding structure, not just the model, carries much of the domain competence.
arxiv-2605-02392:
Valentin Knappich, Anna Hätty, Simon Razniewski, and Annemarie Friedrich make patent novelty prediction fine-grained, at the level of single claim features and the passages that disclose them. Examiners must judge whether an invention is already shown in prior art, a matching task between claim features and document passages. Past work treated novelty as a binary label per claim, which invites spurious correlations and lacks practical detail.

Their data set, FiNE-Patents, holds 3,658 first patent claims annotated with feature-level prior art references drawn from European Search Opinion documents. They propose judging models on a joint retrieval and abstract reasoning task at feature level. A model must identify the specific passages that bear on each feature, not just guess novel or not.
arxiv-2605-02492:
Muhammed H. Güneş and four co-authors ask whether the charge density of a real material can be written directly from a given potential, without solving the full Kohn-Sham equations each time. Model data often feed approximations in density functional theory, a standard method for materials. Here the target is the observable itself, not just a correction term inside the method.

The central building block comes from the response of a uniform electron gas. The team tests a ladder of approximations, from a simple Thomas-Fermi-like form to Taylor expansions and connector theory methods. Tests cover cubic helium, silicon, and aluminum, three very different materials. Accuracy improves step by step with the richer forms, showing how far explicit formulas can go.
arxiv-2605-02992:
Abraham Itzhak Weinberg introduces PHANTOM, a system for making honeytokens that an intruder cannot easily spot as fake. Honeytokens are decoy digital assets, planted to detect and assign blame for unauthorized access. Standard generators produce static, template-based tokens. Such tokens carry no feel for the firm they sit in, and checks on form, meaning, and statistics can expose them as plants.

PHANTOM encodes firm-specific knowledge into its pipeline: domain names, service naming habits, stack idioms, and realistic spreads of secret values. Quality is scored on four parts: valid form, coherent meaning, plausible statistics, and human acceptance. Across eight token types and four firm settings, PHANTOM clearly beat a template baseline on that score. Human judges accepted its tokens far more often, and its tokens resisted detection better.
arxiv-2605-03092:
Gaurav Negi and Paul Buitelaar add structured opinion data to a set of investor micro-blogs so emotion analysis can show what each feeling targets. Sentiment alone says little about why investors feel as they do, and emotion labels alone miss the target as well.

Using a language-model pipeline, they built opinion graphs for sentences from ten thousand StockTwits comments in the StockEmotions dataset. They then test whether adding this opinion structure helps graph neural network classifiers. Their analysis finds classification improves across emotion groups when the opinion semantics are included in the model input.
arxiv-2605-03192:
Kyota Tamano and Keiji Saito sort how entropy production behaves near transitions in chemical reaction networks. Small-system rules for entropy are well known. But its behavior at large-scale transitions out of equilibrium had not been classified.

They study well-mixed networks that can reverse. Noise formulas, normal forms, and Floquet theory yield exponents for four bifurcation types. The exponents cover both fluctuations and responses. A bound in trajectory space then gives a scaling law that links the two. One lesson is sharp. A divergent response needs divergent fluctuations, so fluctuation measures are the sharper probe.
arxiv-2605-03392:
István Gaál gives a practical algorithm for finding all generators of power integral bases in pure quintic fields, a monogenity question in algebraic number theory. Standard tools like Baker's method and lattice reduction still leave many small exponents to check, which can dominate the work.

Gaál adds a sieving idea that sharply cuts the number of remaining small exponents after reduction. With that sieve, all leftover cases can be tested within a few minutes, a surprising speed for this problem class. The trick is general and should speed many similar integral basis computations beyond the quintic case.
arxiv-2605-03492:
Karolina Gorna, Nicolas Iooss, Yannick Seurin, Rida Khatoun, and Keith Makan extend the Zorya concolic framework from TinyGo toys to real binaries. The new target is output from Go's standard compiler. Zorya lifts binaries to an intermediate form. It reasons with an SMT solver over concrete and symbolic values, to find vulnerabilities.

Multi-threaded gc binaries required new steps. Thread states are restored from debugger dumps, runtime preemption is neutralized, and overlay path analysis covers untaken branches. On eleven real flaws in production projects, including Kubernetes and Go-Ethereum, the tool found seven at binary level. One was a silent integer overflow no rival tool caught.
arxiv-2605-03592:
Haoran Zhang and Long Feng develop high-dimensional goodness-of-fit tests for elliptical models, a flexible family of distributions in many variables. After affine standardization, an elliptical distribution should show independence between its radial part and its directional part. Their tests check exactly that, using coordinatewise correlations between the log-radius and the directional parts.

A sum statistic catches dense departures spread over many coordinates, a max statistic catches sparse ones concentrated in a few, and a Cauchy combination adapts between the two. The authors derive the null limits, prove the sum and max parts are asymptotically independent under the null and under certain alternatives, and validate a plug-in standardization step. Simulations show stable size control and clear coordinate-level diagnostics.
arxiv-2605-03692:
Anusrika Datta and Stefan Richter study cyclic vectors in radially weighted Besov spaces, spaces of holomorphic functions on the unit ball whose radial derivatives are square integrable. A vector is cyclic when its multiples under multipliers are dense in the space, so it can approximate everything. Some spaces lack the complete Pick property, which complicates the picture.

For bounded holomorphic functions with no zeros in the ball, the authors give a condition on the logarithm of the function. The condition implies cyclicity. It also yields invertibility properties for the reciprocal in a Smirnov-type class. A comparison principle helps verify the condition: domination by a cyclic function transfers a weaker sequential cyclicity. The results clarify cyclicity where complete Pick methods fail.
arxiv-2605-03792:
Haesung Lee and seven co-authors release TriBench-Ko, a Korean benchmark for the risks of using large language models in judicial work. Existing legal benchmarks lean on proxy tasks such as bar exams. They miss the performance and hazards of daily judicial processes. TriBench-Ko instead builds on verified judicial task needs.

Four core tasks are covered: case law summaries, precedent retrieval, legal issue spotting, and evidence analysis. Each item also probes a risk in use, including hallucination, omission, statutory misapplication, demographic bias, overcompliance, prompt sensitivity, and overreach. Evaluating a range of current models, the authors find frequent significant risks, with models struggling most at precedent retrieval and at capturing key legal information.
arxiv-2605-04092:
Jean-Pierre Magnot develops a pairwise-comparison viewpoint on finite families of qubit states, starting from the transition amplitudes between pure states. He separates three levels of comparison data: the complex amplitudes themselves, the transition probabilities derived from them, and phase-valued pairwise comparisons. The paper works at the level of concepts, aiming to isolate a common language between pairwise comparison theory and basic quantum geometry.

In the non-orthogonal case, the phase data define a reciprocal pairwise comparison structure with values in the circle group. Magnot shows the corresponding triangular defects relate naturally to normalized Bargmann invariants, and therefore to geometric phases, giving inconsistency-type quantities a simple quantum-kinematic reading. He also comments on constraints from Gram matrices of rank at most two. And he comments on passing from unitary phase data to more general transition data.
arxiv-2605-04192:
Hector Giacomini examines a manuscript on special relativity written in 1914 by Conrad Habicht, a close friend of Albert Einstein during their years in Bern. The manuscript seems never to have been published, and the Zurich library ETH-Bibliothek put it online in late 2024.

Habicht gives a clear, teaching-style account of the theory, with much space for the older problems that came before Einstein. Those include the ether, key light experiments, and Lorentz's ideas. Giacomini argues the text shows how Habicht remembered the theory's roots, not just Einstein's famous 1905 paper alone.
arxiv-2605-04792:
Anup Dixit and Sunil Kumar Pasupulati study the genus number of number fields, a measure tied to how ramification affects a field's ideal class group. They focus on fields whose symmetry groups have specific forms, along with pure quartic fields. Knowing how genus numbers spread across a family helps reveal its arithmetic pattern.

The authors establish the statistics for these families and obtain exact results on averages and higher moments for one main family. Based on heuristic reasoning, they also offer a conjecture about families where only a vanishing share of fields should attain any fixed genus number.
arxiv-2605-04992:
Marco Arazzi and four co-authors restore safety behaviour to downloadable model adapters without erasing the expertise those adapters were built to provide. Public repositories host thousands of low-rank adapters, but many arrive without the refusal behaviour responsible training would have given them. Fine-tuning on safety data restores refusals yet damages the specialist skill, and users lack both training corpora.

Their method, NeWTral, translates unsafe adapter weights directly into safety-aligned ones entirely within parameter space. Across four model families, eight professional domains, and scales up to very large models, it cut attack success sharply while keeping most knowledge intact. The fix runs in one pass over the weights.
arxiv-2605-05192:
Ziang Chen and four co-authors test a sharpened triangle inequality for sums of functions proposed by Carbery, in a case study involving the Grok language model. The proposed inequality bounds the size of a sum by pairwise overlap measures between the functions. Some intermediate lemmas in the work were explored with the assistance of a large language model, as the title's case-study framing indicates.

The authors first construct a counterexample showing the inequality fails for every exponent above two. They then prove that if an estimate of this form holds at all, its key exponent is bounded, and at the critical exponent they establish the inequality for all integer cases. A sharp three-function bound with an optimal exponent improves earlier work by other authors.
arxiv-2605-05592:
Asking a model the same question many times and taking the majority answer often improves accuracy. Yi Liu examines exactly when that trick helps, hurts, or flips direction as votes accumulate. Classical theory, assuming a fixed skill level per question, implies a tidy monotone story: above a threshold, more votes always help.

Liu shows the real picture is richer. Under a latent distribution of per-question success probabilities, voting curves can bend repeatedly, even infinitely often in an explicit construction. The full distribution determines the curve, but the curve cannot be run backward to recover the distribution.
arxiv-2605-05692:
Researchers at Chiba University's Graduate School of Informatics tackle a privacy flaw in encrypted video recognition. This task lets machines classify human activity in video without exposing sensitive visual content. Encryption-based methods protect privacy well and keep accuracy high. But they break down when encrypted videos are compressed, and both recognition and visual quality collapse. The team's method, CFE-PPAR, is the first compression-friendly encryption approach for this task.

Videos encrypted with secret keys can be read directly by a video transformer whose settings are transformed with the same keys. Tests on the UCF101 and HMDB51 action sets under Motion-JPEG and H.264 compression show CFE-PPAR beating earlier methods. Authorized clients can still decrypt content for forensic use, so the system guards privacy in transit and storage without surrendering recognition accuracy.
arxiv-2605-05792:
Charmonium, a bound state of a charm quark and its antiparticle, is a delicate probe of hot and cold nuclear matter. Partha Pratim Bhaduri reviews how it is produced in low-energy nuclear collisions, drawing on experiments at CERN, Fermilab, and HERA. Fixed-target proton-nucleus and nucleus-nucleus runs map the interplay of cold-medium effects and hot-medium suppression.

The review then looks forward. Two upcoming facilities, the CBM experiment at FAIR and NA60+ at CERN, will measure charmonium close to its production threshold. Those measurements should sharpen understanding of how the bound states form and dissolve.
arxiv-2605-05892:
Steering a language model by nudging its internal activations sounds elegant, yet large evaluations show simple prompting often beats it. Zehao Jin and four co-authors blame the field's simplifying assumptions: fixed, single-step, position-invariant nudges. Their method, FLAS, learns a flow instead: a velocity field, conditioned on the concept, that transports activations continuously.

The field moves representations along a trajectory rather than jumping them once. That generality addresses why older methods generalized poorly to unseen concepts. The work reframes activation steering as learning how representations should travel, not where a single vector points.
arxiv-2605-05992:
Hongjin Du and Aleksandra Lekić link economic dispatch with converter control in hybrid AC and high voltage DC grids. Huge offshore wind farms feed such grids, yet fixed gain droop controllers struggle when wind output swings hard. Their framework lets system level optimization set the local control gains directly.

Wind forecast errors are modeled zone by zone with Beta distributions that fit low, mid, and high power ranges. A chance constrained stochastic power flow then yields the best droop gain from its first order terms, with no Jacobian needed. Voltage security limits are built into the local control itself. Tests on a four terminal system show the adaptive gains beat fixed ones and cut power tracking errors during extreme wind swings.
arxiv-2605-06092:
Yaozong Zheng and six co-authors teach visual trackers from unlabeled video with a dual context mechanism. Self supervised trackers often model context poorly, and past context methods built on non semantic queries adapt badly when no labels exist. Reliable context cues are the missing piece for learning strong tracking features without annotation.

Their framework pairs fine grained semantic prompts with contextual noise in a two stage design. Early in training, instance patch tokens guide both forward and backward tracking branches while the model picks up basic skill. Noise is then injected step by step, forcing the tracker to build robust features in a harder space. The mechanism runs only during training, so inference stays efficient, and experiments show clear superiority.
arxiv-2605-06292:
Maksim Gladyshev, Natasha Alechina, and Brian Logan show that temporal causal models can serve as a model of computation. Causal models, also called structural equation models, represent how events depend on each other and support reasoning about interventions and counterfactuals. Their temporal extension adds reasoning across time steps, and this paper asks how much computing power that formalism carries in its own right.

The authors prove temporal causal models can encode linear bounded automata, placing them at the level of context sensitive languages. With variables beyond any finite count, the models are Turing complete, matching the strongest standard notion of computation. These results formally connect causal reasoning with classical computation theory. Counterfactual tools from causal inference may therefore transfer into the theory of computation itself, the authors suggest.
arxiv-2605-06492:
W. Chen and eighteen co-authors report fifteen new millisecond pulsars found in 47 Tucanae, one of the largest and closest globular clusters. The cluster hosts many X-ray binaries and pulsars, but its distance meant older surveys caught only the brightest. More pulsars would reveal the cluster's dynamics and might include unusual systems.

Using the sensitive MeerKAT telescope, the team ran two campaigns designed around strong scintillation on this sight line. The finds raise the cluster total to forty-two known pulsars. Highlights include a black widow system spotted as a candidate in 2002 and an eccentric binary with a massive companion, plus fresh locations for two elusive known pulsars.
arxiv-2605-06792:
James Brown and eight co-authors cut noise in quantum simulations of fermionic Hamiltonians using measurements taken mid-circuit. Such simulations are a leading quantum computing application, but deep Trotter circuits accumulate errors on today's hardware. Their framework combines an encoded Trotter synthesis with Clifford noise reduction and Shor-style stabilizer checks enabled by measuring before the circuit ends.

Running a six-qubit encoded step on a barium-based development system, the encoded approach lowers logical error rates by up to fifty-four percent. Deferring the stabilizer readout to the end erases the advantage, proving timely fault detection is the active ingredient. Machine learning also helps pick better verification operators than random choices.
arxiv-2605-06892:
Ernie Chu and Vishal M. Patel cut the cost of video generation by giving different tokens different numbers of denoising steps. Diffusion transformers apply the same step count to every space-time token, although much of a video is redundant motion the eye ignores. Their Heterogeneous Step Allocation method assigns step budgets by each token's velocity dynamics, entirely at inference time with no retraining.

A cache synchronization trick lets active tokens still attend to the full sequence while skipped tokens rest, and a cached update advances resting tokens in one operation. On two video models, for both text- and image-conditioned generation, the method beats prior caching approaches and the standard baseline, holding quality even at a quarter of the usual runtime.
arxiv-2605-06992:
Yonatan Slutzky and four co-authors ask why AI agents that learn new tasks often fail to stay safe on them. An agent may perform an unseen task correctly while mishandling its risks. The authors argue the gap is not only a training flaw; safety itself can make the task-to-behavior mapping more complex.

In a control-theory analysis, adding safety requirements often made the optimal controller change more sharply with the task. Experiments with a simulated quadcopter and a language-model agent in a business setting confirmed the pattern. Imitating safe behavior looked easy on known tasks, but generalizing safely across tasks proved much harder.
arxiv-2605-07192:
Jun Dai and seven co-authors reconstruct sharp 3D scenes from blurry handheld photos with help from event cameras. Popular reconstruction methods fail under severe motion blur, and earlier event-based fixes needed low-resolution sensors in strict sync. Their system pairs ordinary and event cameras at high resolution without requiring tight synchronization.

Sharp images are first recovered from event data, then a geometry transformer estimates camera poses to start the reconstruction. Event-based and consistency losses keep optimization stable and faithful. On a new dataset captured with their rig, plus existing benchmarks, the method achieves leading results and stays robust under heavy blur.
arxiv-2605-07492:
Zhiheng Li and fourteen co-authors built a benchmark to measure how well computers can parse documents into text, formulas, tables, and reading order. Existing benchmarks, they argue, are too narrow to show what current parsers can really do. Their benchmark, PureDocBench, covers ten domains and sixty-six subcategories across nearly fifteen hundred pages.

Each page appears in clean, digitally degraded, and real photographed or shared versions, with annotations checked by automated validation and human review. The team tested fifty-eight models, from pipeline parsers to general vision-language models. The best average score was about eighty out of one hundred, and real-world versions cost models roughly twelve points against clean ones. All data, tools, and evaluation code are public.
arxiv-2605-07792:
Vasilis Niarchos and two co-authors reframe what neural operators are for. These networks are built to learn maps between function spaces. The authors show any finite-dimensional function can be viewed as an operator acting by composition on functions of a helper base space. That reframing turns ordinary fitting into an operator learning problem.

On analytic benchmarks of growing complexity and dimension, neural operators matched or beat multilayer perceptrons and Kolmogorov-Arnold networks while using far fewer parameters and less training time. As a real test, a tensorized Fourier neural operator learned corrections to top nuclear mass models from a partly observed residual field over the nuclear chart. It reached accuracy among the best recent neural approaches. The framework scales from toy functions to structured scientific data.
arxiv-2605-07892:
Ahmad Aloradi and three co-authors make sparse neural network training hit a chosen sparsity target without expensive tuning. Sparsity is usually steered indirectly by a regularization weight whose effect on the final sparsity is hard to predict. For Bregman-based optimizers the team found the same target could need weights differing by a hundredfold between variants. Trial-and-error sweeps were the only route.

Their adaptive scheme updates the weight on the fly from the gap between current and target sparsity. Tested on automatic speaker verification with two architectures and two datasets, it reliably landed targets between seventy-five and ninety-nine percent sparsity. It also converged faster early than an oracle-tuned fixed-weight baseline, matched or beat its final error rate, and kept the robustness advantages of the non-adaptive method.
arxiv-2605-07992:
Jonas Mureika and Elias C. Vagenas compute how quantum gravity changes the maximum entropic force, the idea that gravity itself emerges from entropy gradients. Different uncertainty principles from quantum gravity, the general, extended, and combined variants among them, deform the basic uncertainty relations in different ways. Each should leave its own fingerprint on the entropic force.

They work through several principles, including a linear-quadratic general form, and find the changed force depends on the parameters of whichever principle is assumed, and hence on the quantum gravity theory beneath. In the extended-principle case, the force also depends on the number of Planck areas involved. The work shows how a heat-based view of gravity could, in principle, tell quantum gravity theories apart.
arxiv-2605-08092:
René Kizilcec and colleagues introduce the Million Tutoring Moves project, an open dataset for studying how tutoring works. Tutoring research has long lacked large, shared records of real sessions. The project sits inside the National Tutoring Observatory, an infrastructure built to study authentic tutoring and turn findings into practice.

The first release holds 4,654 math tutoring transcripts from a United States nonprofit online tutoring platform. The team describes the vision behind the collection and its goals: safe, open, large-scale, broad, and multimodal data. Such records can support studies of teaching moves, better tutor training, and AI tools grounded in real educational interaction.
arxiv-2605-08192:
Varad Vishwarupe, Nigel Shadbolt, Marina Jirotka, and Ivan Flechais argue, in a position paper, that the NeurIPS conference should set reproducibility standards for frontier AI safety claims. Such claims now shape deployment choices, governance, and public trust, yet the artifacts needed to check them are routinely withheld.

The authors call this an evidential inversion: the most consequential safety claims are often the least reproducible. They frame non-reproducibility as a failure of evaluation method, not a mere transparency preference, and cite recent safety and transparency reports showing that pre-deployment testing is getting harder. The proposal asks the field's top venue to require checkable evidence.
arxiv-2605-08292:
Molodtsov and two colleagues redesign how sparse mixture of experts models route tokens to specialist networks. Such models scale capacity by sending each token to a few chosen experts, but routers face a trade off between load balance and specialisation. Strong balancing can suppress specialisation, while aggressive diversity often causes routing collapse, where experts stop differentiating.

Their Hi-MoE framework splits routing control into two coupled levels, inter group balancing for fair traffic across expert groups and intra group specialisation for complementary behaviour within groups. Analysis explains how the hierarchical goals reshape the router, promoting stable specialisation and curbing collapse. The method beats recent sparse routing and grouped mixture baselines across language and vision benchmarks, with scaling studies and ablations confirming robustness. In large scale pretraining on 58 billion tokens, Hi-MoE with 7 billion parameters cuts perplexity and improves expert balance over OLMoE of the same size.
arxiv-2605-08392:
Samuel Hurault, Thomas Moreau, and Gabriel Peyré replace worst-case error bounds for diffusion samplers with exact asymptotic formulas. Running a reverse diffusion in few steps makes parameter choices decisive, but classical convergence bounds hide the target's geometry inside pessimistic constants.

The authors expand the Euler-Maruyama weak error and the Fréchet error for small step sizes, with explicit formulas when the data are Gaussian. Those expansions become objectives for tuning the noise schedule, rescaling, and stochasticity level against the target's covariance spectrum. One concrete prediction: the best stochasticity level falls as the step budget shrinks, a rule of thumb practitioners can apply directly.
arxiv-2605-08692:
Beshr IslamBouli and David Jin present AAAC, a fast way to compress language model weights to four bits for cheaper inference. Standard methods map weights onto a fixed grid, while the most accurate rivals need hours of gradient assisted tuning. AAAC instead learns two tiny codebooks per layer and lets each weight group pick whichever codebook rebuilds its output best under real activations.

The codebook choice hides in an unused sign bit, adding no storage at all, and the whole process finishes in minutes on one graphics card. Against seven established methods across model families, AAAC wins on accuracy at a fraction of the tuning time. Efficient deployment gains quality without the wait.
arxiv-2605-08892: Helena Cobo stretches the famed Pascal grid to more than one input. Grid cells hold counts from more than one way splits, tied to sets of points. She works out the traits of these big grids. She proves the vast grid built from whole count points sits in the multivariate Riordan group, a clan of vast grids with its own times rule. Group rank opens known tools for work with the grid. The tie links a stock count object to new Riordan work.
arxiv-2605-09192:
Zhou and nine colleagues argue agent skills should be distilled from evidence, not advance plans. Skills, the guides that steer agents, can greatly raise task success, but their quality is hard to judge without environment checks. Existing methods lean on preference logs instead of direct environment contact, often giving weak or degraded gains.

The team identifies a timing bottleneck: robust skills should be evidence based, distilled from real contact rather than prior plans. They introduce the Posterior Distillation Index, a path level metric judging how firmly a distilled skill rests on evidence. To compute it, they present SPARK, which generates environment checked paths and applies the index as a live diagnostic signal. Across 86 runnable tasks, SPARK skills beat no skill baselines and top human written skills on student models, at lower cost than teachers. The findings show index guided distillation produces efficient, portable skills grounded in real contact.
arxiv-2605-09692:
Jia introduced causal state binding, a test of whether a language agent's actions truly follow its stated state: traces, memories, plans, and constraints. Current evaluations rarely check that link. The framework intervenes on the decisive state while hiding the intervention target from the model's prompt, then checks whether actions shift with the decisive state yet ignore irrelevant cues.

Across 57,816 scored records in seven corpus units, the structured-agent setup beat high-randomness controls and targeted component removals on reason, memory, veto, and self-continuity. On 300 SWE-bench Lite issues, adding an oracle-free state-binding score lifted issue-to-file hit@3 AUC from 0.873 to 0.935. The paper offers a positive yardstick: good agents act from their state, not around it.
arxiv-2605-09892:
Xie and six colleagues revisit a simplifying assumption behind low Earth orbit satellite-to-ground laser links: that twinkling from turbulence and pointing loss vary independently. Both effects share one cause, atmospheric turbulence, and the usual split also blurs the distinct roles of the free atmosphere and the boundary layer near the ground. For laser links that must dump large data volumes in short passes, that shortcut can mislead link design.

Their replacement is a state-coupled joint fading model, in which a discrete slow atmospheric state, scaled separately for the free atmosphere and boundary layer, ties scintillation and angular loss together. Conditioning on the state keeps the maths tractable and yields a closed-form outage probability. Numbers show the independent baseline can misjudge outage under layered turbulence, with the bias shifting by elevation as geometry changes which loss dominates.
arxiv-2605-09992:
Eldenk and five colleagues identified attention drift in speculative decoding, where a small drafter model drafts future tokens to accelerate inference. Drafter models degrade sharply under template perturbation and long-context inputs. The paper traces a new phenomenon: as the drafter generates each new token, attention slowly moves from the prompt onto its own recently generated tokens.

Across both EAGLE3 drafters and MTP heads, drift appears to be a property of drafter designs. The cause is the unnormalized residual path between chain steps. The drafter's hidden-state magnitude grows ever larger with chain depth, acting like extra pre-norm transformer layers on the target, not a standalone autoregressive predictor. Two fixes improved acceptance length: post-norm on drafter states and per-state RMSNorm on captured target states. Gains reached up to 2 times under template perturbation, 1.18 times on long-context tasks, and 1.10 times on seven benchmarks.
arxiv-2605-10592:
Vipin Singh and five colleagues build a tough monitoring system for sewer overflows. Old combined sewer systems in many cities are stressed by heavy rain, which can trigger overflows dumping raw wastewater with serious harm to nature and public health. Forecasting how fast overflow basins fill is key to spotting when they will overtop. Their 2026 paper presents a web demo.

The demo pairs deep learning forecasts in cloud and edge settings in a live monitoring dashboard that keeps working when networks fail. It shows early-warning signals and overflow risk signs from filling-level forecasts, in normal cloud mode and in limited edge mode during outages. The system gives clear risk news to sewer operators, city managers, and others, aiding informed, accountable choices in safety-critical work.
arxiv-2605-10792:
Yesom Park, Eric Gelphman, Stanley Osher, and Samy Wu Fung offer a 2026 neural method for optimal transport, the task of reshaping one distribution of data into another at least cost. Existing neural approaches juggle rival networks and unstable min-max training, so the authors rebuild the problem around a single potential function from the Kantorovich dual.

They recast the key transform as a fixed-point problem solved with proximal steps, which keeps the solution feasible by construction and lets gradients flow without differentiating through the inner loop. Tests on high-dimensional Gaussians, physical data, and image translation show strong accuracy with steadier training and lower memory use. Researchers get one network that yields both forward and backward maps and extends to class-by-class settings.
arxiv-2605-10992:
G.G.L. Nashed studies how higher-curvature corrections in f(R, G) gravity shift black-hole photon spheres and shadows. Working in a static, spherically symmetric spacetime, the analysis expands field equations in small couplings tied to quadratic curvature invariants, perturbing the Schwarzschild solution.

Analytic expressions show higher-curvature corrections shift unstable photon orbits, and the Gauss-Bonnet part shifts them more than mixed-curvature parts do. Those shifts propagate into the shadow radius, with photon-sphere displacement and direct metric changes playing distinct roles. Strong lensing and quasinormal modes gain sensitivity to the corrections. Gravity researchers get a consistent leading-order map of how modified gravity would bend black-hole light.
arxiv-2605-11092:
Linmu Qiao, Zhichun Ouyang, and Sisi Zhou turn a punctured surface code into a distributed sensor for many-body Hamiltonians, estimating a weighted average of coupling strengths rather than each coupling separately. All Z-type couplings in their protocol correspond to the same nontrivial logical Z operator of the code.

On a planar patch with two X-cut holes, disjoint couplings reduce to a global witness condition. A closed dual loop intersects every chain an odd number of times, plus a local clean-opening condition. Together these give a concrete construction where all signal chains implement the same logical operator. For three-body interactions with overlapping supports, the team identifies the applicable interaction class. Quantum sensing teams get a noise-robust distributed protocol with topological design criteria.
arxiv-2605-11492: Johnny Corbino proposes a single-shot, training-free detector for adversarial image perturbations based on high-order mimetic operators. Standard FGSM and PGD attacks add tiny high-frequency sign patterns that fool deep classifiers while staying small in size. With no retraining, no surrogate classifier and without access to the network under attack, the detector judges the input alone in linear time. On the peppers test image it separates attacked inputs from clean ones by up to fivefold, while smooth perturbations stay within one percent of clean.
arxiv-2605-11692: Roni Muslim studies triplet major-rule shifts with joint flip on quenched networks. Triplets of one agent and two neighbours meet, while flip acts only on agreed triplets, splitting agreement from shocks. Quenched layout shifts the order-chaos key point away from the well-mixed value. For Barabási-Albert, Erdős-Rényi, regular and Watts-Strogatz networks, key exponents stay near mean-field values, hinting a common pattern. The strongest shift occurs for Watts-Strogatz networks, where clumping weakens the ordered phase, though relink brings back steadiness.
arxiv-2605-11792: Zoltan Nagy and Davison Soper formulate parton shower evolution beyond leading order for electron-positron annihilation. Parton showers follow a renormalization group equation reflecting infrared perturbative QCD with color, spin, and quantum interference. Splitting functions existed only to leading order, so the authors build a framework reaching order alpha-s squared. This requires representing Feynman graphs with off-shell partons carrying vector or spinor labels instead of on-shell spins.
arxiv-2605-11892: Emir Sezik and Gunnar Pruessner study tipping-point dynamics in conserved systems with one-way coupling. They look at two n-part order fields where one-way influence enters only through nonlinear links between species. A one-loop renormalization-group study shows tipping behavior hinges on microscopic values. For n of 4 or more, a fixed point appears where dynamics obey detailed balance over long scales. Conservation also cuts the count of free scaling exponents.
arxiv-2605-12192: Ge Yan and three colleagues design antenna placement using long-term, cell-wide channel statistics. Most designs chase short-term channel data, forcing frequent channel estimation and antenna moves. Their framework optimizes antenna spots over a timescale from base-station statistics, with a cell-specific model for multiuser systems. A covariance-eigenvalues-balancing design then nears spots by cutting user channel correlation, using only the base-station angular power spectrum. Simulations on urban layouts show gains over fixed antennas, nearing the bound of instant designs for mid-size regions.
arxiv-2605-12692: Maassarani asks when finite quandle representations break into irreducible pieces. A finite-dimensional map with a unit inner product always decomposes into irreducibles, but not all maps share that property. He proves a finite-dimensional map of a finite quandle over the complex numbers decomposes into irreducibles exactly when every element in its image is diagonalisable. An irreducible map is unitary for some inner product exactly when every image element has determinant of modulus one. Twisting by a character yields an irreducible map with a unit inner product.
arxiv-2605-13092: Zhang and Deng bring pretraining to kernel density estimation in high dimensions, where classic kernel smoothing struggles to pick kernels that fit each spot. Their pretrained neural network recommends a suitable kernel for each sample point, making efficient adaptive estimation possible. Numerical tests show large accuracy gains when the target distribution resembles the pretraining family. When the target differs substantially, gains dilute but return with an extra fine-tuning step.
arxiv-2605-13392: Asaf Lev-Ran, Pavel Arkhipov and Vladimir Kolmogorov propose a tighter way to solve MAP-MRF inference. That task chooses discrete variable values that minimise a sum of single-variable and pairwise costs. The usual approach solves a linear programming relaxation and then strengthens it by adding clusters of variables. Their technique finds such clusters by running singleton arc consistency, a constraint-propagation check, on a related constraint problem. Experiments indicate the new tightening beats the earlier frustrated-cycle search of Sontag and colleagues.
arxiv-2605-13492: Zirui Kong, Youqian Zhang and Sze Yiu Chau expose a security hole in robot touch sensing. Robots rely on tactile sensors to handle objects safely, yet the safety of touch sensing has barely been studied. The authors target Hall-effect fingertip sensors with intentional electromagnetic interference. A crafted signal injection creates phantom forces, raising sensed force more than ninefold and shifting its direction by 65 degrees. Such shifts can paralyse learning-based touch classification and push a robot hand to crush fragile objects or drop dangerous loads.
arxiv-2605-13692: Yuetai Li and eight colleagues show regret in online learning over combinatorial actions is governed by polyhedral instability, the number of active-region changes. Under full information feedback and fixed partitions, they prove regret equals theta of the square root of one plus region switches times horizon times log max vertices. For online submodular-concave games under Lovász convexification, that reduces to the permutation-switch count with a matching rate. Tests on synthetic and real combinatorial problems validate the predicted scaling.
arxiv-2605-13792: Efe İzbudak and Kadri İlker Berktav construct, for every integer s and every n of at least 1, a symmetric monoidal (infinity,n)-category Leg_n^s. Its objects are s-shifted contact derived Artin stacks and its i-morphisms are i-fold Legendrian correspondences. The construction rests on an s-shifted contact structure being an s-shifted symplectic structure relative to B G_m. For an s-shifted contact stack X, they obtain the derived Legendrian category F_c(X).
arxiv-2605-13892: Nahid Binandeh Dehaghani and four colleagues propose a QPINN frame with a quantum tuned code for the lid-driven cavity problem. Their path uses a quantum neural network to learn quantum feature maps coding space points. A tuned quantum circuit processes them within a physics-aware loss form. Number tests show their QNN-TE-QPINN shows stable training ways and rival answer hits versus old physics-aware neural networks and hybrid quantum models using old codes.
arxiv-2605-14292: Sun and three co-authors study KV-cache compression at small budgets, testing seven mechanisms. Tests run on mathematical reasoning at budgets 64 and 128. All seven mechanisms were rejected. The team proposes alpha, a change to the TriAttention scorer replacing argmax-top-k with greedy facility selection under a V-space redundancy penalty with weight lambda. At lambda 0.5, alpha clears Bonferroni on two of four cells, with no cell negative.
arxiv-2605-14492: Takemoto gives a theory for adversarial synchronisation control in Kuramoto nets, where small repeated phase kicks can raise or lower collective sync. The Ott-Antonsen reduction gives a closed-form rule for one kick's effect on order. Each kick gives a finite, coupling-free order shift even when sync is weak. Slow settling near critical coupling and mean-field feedback explain the boost. Fixed-point analysis shows a rise-fall asymmetry with noise-driven fall escape. For nets, the theory splits kick sensitivity from mean-field dominance.
arxiv-2605-15192: Katherine Freese, Evangelos I. Sfakianakis, and Barmak Shams Es Haghi examine axion dark matter when the inflaton couples straight to gluons. That coupling can raise the QCD confinement scale during that era, making the axion temporarily heavy and damping isocurvature ripples. As it proceeds that scale relaxes, the axion lightens, and late ripples can supply the seen dark matter. The mechanism selects plateau-like inflation over monomial models, which let that scale grow too fast.
arxiv-2605-15392: Megan Birch and four others offer FRIES, a neuromorphic framework for picky surveillance with event-based cameras. Such cameras report pixel radiance changes at microsecond resolution with high dynamic range, but their sparse asynchronous output needs event-space methods. FRIES gates out background noise, pools events into motion maps, clusters regions of focus, and extracts leading tones per region to tell apart ordered marks like rotor rotation from clutter. A tuned time surface then shows targets by phase coherence with those tones.
arxiv-2605-15592: Tung Do, Thuan Hoang Nguyen, and Hao Li speed up few-step image generation. Sphere Encoder makes fine images in few steps but flips between pixel space and latent space. It trains rebuild and generation in one net, which pits the two goals. Their split uses a fixed pretrained encoder plus a separate denoising model trained wholly in a spherical latent space. No pixel-space hops recur in training. Rebuild and generation can now specialize apart. On animal faces, flowers, and ImageNet it beats Sphere Encoder on quality and speed.
arxiv-2605-15892: David Porfirio and five colleagues examine the emerging robot-wrangler role, the person who sets up, oversees, and fixes robots in hospitals, museums, and warehouses. A scoping review yields a typology of wrangling across the literature. That label covers a complex, mixed set of activities that resists clear description and support. Drawing on their firsthand and imagined wrangling work, the authors propose design implications for helping individual wranglers and the broader services around them.
arxiv-2605-16092: Vanhaecke gives a new, more transparent proof of Drinfeld's representability theorem, a cornerstone of geometric p-adic Hodge theory. Proved in the 1970s, the theorem says a moduli problem of deformations by quasi-isogenies of certain p-divisible groups is representable by an explicit semi-stable model of the p-adic symmetric space. The notes also present Drinfeld's moduli space and the formal model in detail. Together, the proof and presentation clarify a central result of the field.
arxiv-2605-16392: Xing and eight others present MIST, a plug-in replacement for the projection layer in multiple instance learning for whole-slide pathology images. Standard projection layers rely on morphology alone, limiting endpoints like biomarker status and survival that depend on molecular state not fully visible in H&E stains. MIST uses paired spatial transcriptomics during training only to build virtual molecular stains, clustering gene expression into cross-modal prototypes anchored in frozen feature space. It needs no transcriptomics at inference and improves 240 of 256 configurations, with an average gain of 3.5 percent.
arxiv-2605-16592: Hernández-Hernández, Morales-Técotl and Sánchez-Herrera compute quantum corrections to cosmic ripples on a bouncing universe background from loop quantum cosmology. Tracking second-order quantum spreads and correlations, they find the leading change to the curvature power spectrum is tiny. It scales with the sixth power of wavenumber times the Planck length, and it fits observations. After the bounce, gravitational quantum effects damp the scalar signal, while cross-correlations can destabilize high wavenumbers.
arxiv-2605-16692: Evers and colleagues present EfficientTDMPC, a model-based reinforcement-learning method for continuous control built on the TD-MPC family. A planner seeks action sequences that maximize expected return, but learned models and value networks both inject error. The method averages values across rollout depths and across an ensemble of dynamics heads, and adds pessimistic reanalysis for tasks that can end early. It reaches a strong baseline's final performance with 57% fewer environment steps on HumanoidBench and the DeepMind Control Suite.
arxiv-2605-16792: Yu studies static electromagnetic Love tensors of 5D Myers-Perry black holes through split master equations for field and gravity perturbations. In the static limit, charge response reduces to a massless scalar case, while magnet response and gravity effects yield Heun cases for angular and radial parts. Those Heun cases admit exact answers via special functions. Using tweaked sphere waves, higher spin modes respond to lower-spin sources, and the tidal Love tensor showing that mixing can be found step by step.
arxiv-2605-16892: Artham's team proposes DriveSafe, a system for risk spotting and safety tips in driving. Zero-shot multi-mode models still trail narrow methods on fine-grained, space-grounded risk review. It first makes grounded captions rich with motion, spatial, and depth cues. Those captions drive risk review, naming risky objects, spots, and implied unsafe acts, plus safety tips. Caption-risk pairings fine-tune a lightweight adapter, adding domain knowledge to the base model. On DRAMA, it reaches state-of-the-art scores, with tests backing key choices.
arxiv-2605-17192: Kráčmar and colleagues, including Švihra, report the first fabricated and tested segmented 4H-silicon-carbide low-gain avalanche detectors, sensors prized for radiation hardness and heat tolerance. Strip detectors and pixel arrays with pitches down to 55 micrometers were built with several isolation designs. Beam tests at ELI ERIC showed clean charge separation between neighboring strips with internal gain.
arxiv-2605-17592: James Tian studies ordered discrete POVMs through a residual transform. One use replaces each coordinate by its post-failure effect, appending remaining mass as a terminal outcome. Iterating the transform yields a collapsed POVM with non-escape coordinates as surviving original effects. The collapse map gives a matching link on ordered realizations. Its range holds collapsed POVMs with orthogonal non-escape parts summing to the identity, while fibers hold cases sharing seen squeezes. After collapse, non-escape coordinates stay fixed, while remaining dynamics live in the escape effect.
arxiv-2605-17792: Zhi Li and six colleagues ask whether frontier language-model agents can replace human experts at tuning hydrologic models. They test nine frontier agents on the CREST model used by the US National Weather Service for flash-flood forecasts. Best scores across four held-out gauges range from negative 0.16 to 0.75 on Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency, and no model matches the human expert except Opus-4.7 on one gauge. The gap, they argue, is weak domain grounding, not model size. Their HydroAgent fine-tunes Qwen3-4B on 2,576 expert tuning runs with simulator feedback.
arxiv-2605-18092: Alessandro Celestini and four colleagues rebuild a synthetic urban population from census and survey data, linked by stable social ties, to simulate epidemic spread in a typical medium-size Italian city. They split contacts into daily household contacts and other frequent contacts, plus rare chance meetings between any pair. Age-structured contact patterns speed outbreaks and widen their reach, while letting contact frequency fall with distance barely changes results. Early signs show hierarchical spatial spread, with two regimes in low- and high-density areas.
arxiv-2605-18392: Luca Previdi and Francesco Albarelli derive ultimate precision limits for estimating parameters in time-dependent quantum systems under general Markovian noise. Their 2026 work extends a minimization-over-purifications approach to time-varying channels, giving a differential bound on quantum Fisher information that semidefinite programming can compute. They prove a universal long-time scaling law: in one regime noisy scaling matches the noise-free scaling, while in the other it falls one power of time short. Their error-correction constructions meet the bounds.
arxiv-2605-18492: A. O. Makarenko and five co-authors present, in a 2026 paper, a tool for simulating S-parameters of general multilayer boxed printed circuit boards. The method combines the 2.5D method of moments with a scattering-matrix algorithm, deriving the full dyadic Green's function for a layered waveguide. Surface rooftop, volume pulse, and linear basis functions model planar layers and vertical interconnects. Two numerical examples validate the method, which extends to other bases and shapes.
arxiv-2605-18592: Peilin Wu and six co-authors present AMARIS, a 2026 memory-augmented rubric improvement system for rubric-based reinforcement learning. Rubrics usually update from local evidence like the current batch, discarding diagnostic information from training. AMARIS stores rollout analyses, step summaries, and rubric update records in persistent evaluation memory, then retrieves recent and relevant history to revise rubrics. Across science, medicine, instruction following, and creative writing it beats static, local-adaptive, and memory-ablated baselines, gaining 2.8 points on GPQA-Diamond and 2.2 on IFBench.
arxiv-2605-18992: Marjorie Decleir and eighteen colleagues summarize discussion sessions of the fifth Pandust conference, The Dusty Universe 2025, held in Tucson in November 2025. The meeting brought the dust field together to review progress, hear new results and plan future work across observations, theory, models and laboratory studies. Topics spanned interstellar and circumstellar dust, dust in galaxies, the dust lifecycle and future needs, with emphasis on JWST and ALMA results and on nanodust including PAHs. The document records the main questions, conclusions, challenges, fixes and open questions from November 12 breakout sessions.
arxiv-2605-19192: Guijia Zhang and two colleagues define hallucination-to-action conversion, where a false claim enables a special action. Their evidence-carrying agents treat model text as off-limits, split tool calls into action-key checks, obtain typed proofs, and allow only backed rights through a gate. Red-teaming across 17 groups shows four fixes are each needed; after fixes, standard gate bypass is zero in 1,700 attempts. With content-derived proofs the system shows zero unsafe runs on 200 tasks and 120 browser tasks, while naive agents let bare claims reach unsafe runs.
arxiv-2605-19392: Feng, Ou and Wang derive differential equations that capture the continuous-time behavior of Adam-DA, the descent-ascent cousin of Adam used for zero-sum games. Theory for this popular method has lagged behind practice. The equations closely track the discrete steps of Adam-DA and give a workable analytic frame for studying local convergence and implicit gradient regularization. Their analysis finds the two momentum parameters play exactly opposite roles to their documented effects in minimization problems. GAN experiments across architectures and datasets confirm the reversed momentum effect.
arxiv-2605-19492: Schmidt and Langer build a prototype of a building acoustics test facility predicting sound transmission loss under DIN EN ISO 10140. Early design benefits from estimating how material and geometry choices affect loss in single- and double-leaf walls, insulated or not. Geometry and mesh come from SALOME 9.14, while in-house code elPaSo assembles and solves the model, verified against COMSOL 6.3 on a small-scale facility. Loss estimates for three specimens in one-third-octave bands from 8 Hz to 630 Hz show the insulated double-leaf wall matching theory.
arxiv-2605-19792: Schaumlöffel, Vilas and Roig investigate how vision-language models locate objects, a process far less studied than classification. Probing LLaVA-1.5 and InternVL-3.5 with ablations, attention knockout and causal mediation, they find a containerisation mechanism: object-aligned tokens set the spatial extent, while token order inside barely matters for the predicted box. Only a tiny set of attention heads carries the causal effect for both tasks, early-mid layers for LLaVA and mid-late for InternVL. The two tasks share early steps but then rely on largely separate specialised heads.
arxiv-2605-19992: Yongchun Bi and three co-workers align multi-agent systems ruled by parabolic partial differential equations under seen and unseen disturbances. From boundary outputs alone, an observer estimates seen Dirichlet boundary disturbances while staying robust to unseen upsets inside the domain. Local control laws built from the reference signal and local outputs then drive every agent to track the reference path. Fast tracking follows when unseen upsets vanish, and input-to-state stability holds for the closed loop in all cases.
arxiv-2605-20092: Nilanjana Datta proves two concentration results for quantum sources close to iid, under the widest weakly almost iid condition. Weakly almost iid sources have fixed marginals converging on average to powers of a reference state in tensor form, while correlations and entanglement stay arbitrary. She proves a weak law of large numbers for observables and a universal entropy-concentration principle on subspaces of exponential dimension set by the reference state's von Neumann entropy. These results unify proofs of universal compression and quantum hypothesis-testing bounds beyond the iid setting.
arxiv-2605-20492: Baez, Breton, and Cabrera-Munguia examine energy extraction from a charged black hole wrapped in a magnetic field. They use the electric version of the Penrose process for this study. The field creates a zone where particles can carry negative energy, so a splitting particle can leave one fragment trapped. The other fragment then escapes with extra energy, and the field can switch extraction on or off.
arxiv-2605-20892: Enhui Yu and four colleagues present FruitEnsemble, a multimodal-guided arbitration system for fine-grained fruit spotting. Fine-grained fruit sorting is hard in agricultural computer vision. It is hindered by scarce high-quality datasets and high visual similarity between classes. Their dataset holds 306 fruit categories with 116,233 samples. It first builds a validation-calibrated weighted ensemble of diverse backbones to make a robust top-three candidate pool, then triggers expert review when confidence falls below 0.6.
arxiv-2605-20992: Hao Xu and four colleagues ask whether everyday open-world monocular videos could yield reusable 4D hand-object interaction primitives. Such primitives would cover jointed hand motion, object form with 6D pose over time, and the when and where of contact. Reconstructing hand-object interaction from challenging monocular videos remains hard, since methods often presume known objects or curated scenes. Separately estimated hands and objects also misalign easily under clutter, occlusion, and unseen object geometries, so Open-CHOIR uses contact as an explicit coupling signal.
arxiv-2605-21092: C. Gerlach, Daniel Schmitt, and Pedro Schwaller link intergalactic magnetic fields and gravitational waves through axion magnetogenesis. Finding dark matter options that make multiple observable cosmic signatures is a key goal linking particle physics with future sightings. Axion-like particles linked to the Standard Model photon give a promising design. In the trapped mismatch process, axion swings are delayed, causing cooling in the early cosmos, leading to fast photon making via tachyonic instability and strong helical fields.
arxiv-2605-21192: Marco Gregnanin and colleagues ask if graph neural nets truly help stock-style forecasts. Most tools read only how a series moves over time. Their Time-Geometric model also reads shape patterns in the data, caught by graph neural nets. In wide tests on single-series forecasts, the shape-aware model did clearly better, and the gain passed stats tests.
arxiv-2605-21292: Krishnakumar Balasubramanian studies large-step training dynamics of a two-factor linear transformer model. Unbiased stochastic gradients match the full gradient on average while changing finite-step stability. In one-layer linear self-attention for in-context linear regression, shared-mode mini-batch training reduces to a random two-factor map. The full-batch map preserves an elliptic region, while sampled curvature creates batch-dependent stability edges whose fluctuation drifts the edge outward.
arxiv-2605-21492: Drake Caraker, Bryan Arnold, and David Rhoads prove the attribution impossibility: no feature ranking is faithful, stable, and complete under collinearity. For collinear pairs, ranking amounts to a coin flip. They prove it, measure it across four model classes, and resolve it via ensemble averaging called DASH. They machine-verify it with three hundred five Lean 4 theorems. Exactly two method families exist: faithful-complete methods that are unstable, and ensemble methods like DASH that are stable, reporting ties for symmetric features.
arxiv-2605-21792: Jiongli Zhu and co-authors present DivSkill-SQL, building complementary Text-to-SQL ensembles without fine-tuning. Ensembles draw several candidates and pick one, but power is capped by Pass@K, the chance a candidate is right. Heuristic diversity leaves sets full of correlated failures. Each new skill learns from examples the ensemble misses, targeting its marginal Pass@K contribution. On Spider2-Lite the method lifts accuracy by up to eleven point one points on Snowflake and eight point three on BigQuery. Single-dialect skills transfer without retraining.
arxiv-2605-22092: Zhenrong Gu and co-authors present Astragalus, a tool for automatic configuration repair in production networks. Configuration errors can cause catastrophic service outages, and existing repair tools follow a semantics-driven approach, modeling network semantics as SMT constraints, solved for an error location or fix. Building and solving such constraints is complex, so Astragalus differs, repairing every incident across several sizes of a synthesized network and 97.5 percent of incidents on a real network, with 15 error types, in an average of 6.93 seconds, plus valid repairs under 6 minutes for 7 recent real incidents.
arxiv-2605-22292: Rajapitamahuni and colleagues stabilise a hidden-phase-like metallic state in 1T-TaS2 at equilibrium. Ultrafast pulses can reach this state, but it differs from the insulating ground state and normally vanishes. In exfoliated flakes of intermediate thickness, it lasts up to room temperature. It then passes through a different sequence of transitions. It hosts a metallic band with Fermi-level weight and keeps the star-of-David folding gaps. This offers a platform for steering competing states in layered materials.
arxiv-2605-22492: Cavada, Pelosin and Faggi propose a training-free two-stage framework for mushroom segmentation in low-data settings. SAM3 first produces mushroom masks using macro-taxonomic prompts. DINOv3 then assigns labels through prototype matching in embedding space. A simple transformation of the DINOv3 feature space improves classification. Compared with class-specific prompting, the approach scales better and keeps segmentation cost low. Results span one-shot to few-hundred-shot regimes, giving, to the authors' knowledge, the first baseline for fine-grained semantic segmentation in low-data settings.
arxiv-2605-22692: Moser, Chen and Andreou build a math framework for tracing how hidden variables drive extreme events in partly seen random systems. They combine data assimilation with information based and path based checks to infer hidden precursors from observations, gauge their uncertainty, and track how influence flows toward observed extremes. Filter versus smoother outputs flag onset, while event based hidden state patterns expose trigger paths and distinct cause classes. Three worked cases, from sudden bursts to topographic blocking patterns, show it separating damping driven, forcing driven and mixed pathways.
arxiv-2605-22892: Deprez, Verbeke, and Verdonck test TabPFN for motor insurance pricing. TabPFN is a tabular foundation model that infers from new data without dataset-specific fitting or tuning. Against linear models and XGBoost on two liability datasets, it trailed the linear model on claim frequency. Results there depended on in-context set size. On scarcer claim severity data it matched rivals, but its inference ran far slower. The verdict: promising for sparse data, not yet a replacement for actuarial methods.
arxiv-2605-23092: Avelino and Doronin establish local well-posedness in L2 for the Zakharov-Kuznetsov equation with a linear drift term, posed on a half-strip with nonzero boundary values. Their proof uses Bourgain-type spaces tuned to the ZK dispersive structure, together with directional smoothing and edge estimates. The result gives a solid short-time existence theory for this model on a half-strip shape.
arxiv-2605-23292: Trauthwein and Yukich sharpen second-order Poincaré inequalities for functionals of a Poisson measure, using the Malliavin-Stein method to bound normal approximation in Kolmogorov and Wasserstein distance. Their rates need fewer error terms than earlier results. When a functional sums score functions close to short-range scores, they derive Berry-Esseen bounds under a broad bounded Lipschitz localization condition that allows unbounded score interactions. The approach covers local U-statistics, functionals on hyperbolic space, and space-time Poisson settings including birth-growth models and Laguerre tessellations.
arxiv-2605-23492: Park and colleagues study twist-angle locking in double-moiré trilayers of hexagonal boron nitride and graphene, using large atomistic relaxations. In twisted trilayer boron nitride, matched twist angles create local energy minima with torque sign reversals that pull the system back toward commensuration, though zero twist stays globally stable. In graphene and boron nitride stacks, the global minimum can sit at the commensurate angle near 0.6 degrees. Mismatched structures lose stabilization and gain superlubricity, and electrostatic forces strengthen the locking without changing its physics.
arxiv-2605-23692: O'Gara and colleagues present a tutorial on trajectory-based tuning with adaptive_ts, an open-source Python package for tuning random models. Tuning model inputs to match seen data is a key step in model design and checking. Trajectory-based tuning needs no guesses about model repeat behavior and excels at finding paths through errors between model and seen data, with Bayes tuning. Disease models motivate the work, as shown by the COVID-19 pandemic. The tutorial includes worked examples on a companion webpage.
arxiv-2605-23892: Zheng and five colleagues offer a two-step way to cut the cost of visual geometry transformers, systems that rebuild three-dimensional scenes from many photos at once. Their method first keeps only the most varied frames, then drops spare tokens inside those frames, guided by how attention spreads across layers. Tests on scenes of 500 images ran over 85 percent faster while matching or beating the usual accuracy, suggesting lean token choice can scale these models.
arxiv-2605-23992: Li and seven co-authors model how radiologists read images, not their conclusions. Their system, GazeWorld, treats images as worlds and fixations as a path through them. It predicts the next patch from earlier ones, while a second branch covers unvisited regions. At test time it builds patch sequences from the image alone, needing no gaze data. Frozen GazeWorld features led diagnostic accuracy on nine settings across three chest benchmarks and topped zero-shot accuracy on all three. It also beat a purpose-built gaze model without gaze training.
arxiv-2605-24192: Niedoba, Zwartsenberg, and Wood unify math models of diffusion generalization under Filtered Posterior Mean Collections. Cleaning networks in diffusion models behave alike across designs and settings, and recent work models their outputs by mixing training patches weighted by odds. The authors define the unified class through query sharpness vectors, response weights, and source pools, showing earlier methods emerge from choices. Soft easing of patch methods and grown source pools each improve results, and applied to a known set, the findings yield gains across three natural image data sets.
arxiv-2605-24292: Ivanov and five co-authors introduce TUBE, a tangent upper bound on evidence for discrete diffusion models. Log-likelihood is standard for judging generative models, but discrete diffusion models admit no exact computation. TUBE is a variational upper bound on log-likelihood with an unbiased Monte Carlo estimator. It extends across latent-variable models including masked diffusion, any-order autoregressive models, and block variants. Applied to block masked-diffusion and block any-order models, TUBE shows they sit below the exact autoregressive baseline, so autoregressive models still dominate in likelihood.
arxiv-2605-24492: Wen Ma and colleagues introduce Med-R2, a 2026 benchmark that tests whether medical vision-language models reason from visible evidence or lean on misleading cues. Its stepwise questions follow four clinical stages, with adversarial tweaks probing robustness at each step. The set spans 42,432 images, 31 task types, and 110,406 question-answer pairs. Across 14 models, scores fell stage by stage, yet fine-tuning on the stepwise data markedly improved reasoning robustness.
arxiv-2605-24592: Yusen Feng and colleagues present MuGen, a 2026 data-driven framework for teaching humanoid robots many locomotion skills from example motions. Vector-quantized autoencoders trained with model-based reinforcement learning build a generative representation of locomotion from hours of varied human data. A teacher-student setup with a policy distillation strategy turns that representation into a deployable student policy. The robot then tracks and mimics unseen human motions, and can put the learned latent space to work on other tasks.
arxiv-2605-24792: Ojonugwa Oluwafemi Ejiga Peter and co-authors tackle gut endoscopy AI with a dual-pipeline model that tunes few parameters. Shortages of labeled data, strict privacy rules, and costly tuning limit clinical diagnosis. One pipeline answers clinical questions about images with the Florence-2 vision-language model, cutting training cost. The other uses Low-Rank Adaptation with Stable Diffusion to make synthetic gut images without exposing patient data. On the Kvasir-VQA set, the question-answering model reaches a ROUGE-1 score of 0.92.
arxiv-2605-24892: Baolu Li and co-authors introduce X-Foresight, a world model inside a vision-language-action architecture. Naive next-frame forecasts fail twice: redundant video tokens make forecasts degenerate into trivial copying, and dense forecasts cannot model long causality efficiently. X-Foresight predicts distant chunks rather than nearby frames, dodging trivial copying, keeping dense frames within chunks and sparse jumps between chunks. Training extends prediction horizons gradually, focusing supervision on safety-critical chunks. Tests show it beats vision-language-action baselines in planning while keeping strong fidelity.
arxiv-2605-24992: Changling Li leads an energy-aware multi-agent learning model for mission drone networks. Multi-agent learning already serves driving and smart-city tasks, and drones add trajectory planning. Dynamic settings and tight batteries still block efficient teamwork. The model uses Deep Q-Networks with individual rewards tied to progress and remaining battery. Simulations compare it with shared-reward learning to probe credit. It holds at least four-fifths success regardless of task place and length, and scales better as settings grow, winning more often in fewer steps.
arxiv-2605-25092: Aojie Yuan, Haiyue Zhang, and Shahin Nazarian build AgentIR, a retrieval system tuned for chat agents that must recall long conversations under tight time limits. For each query it chooses among fusion methods. It also decides, from the cheap BM25 ranking alone, whether a slower dense search is worth running. On one benchmark it skips 63 percent of dense searches without losing judged accuracy. On another it skips them all, lifting shared-server capacity from about 154 to roughly 1,400 agents.
arxiv-2605-25192: Nadia Kevine Kouonang, Jeanne Sandrine Takam Mabekou, Thierry Njougouo, and Timoteo Carletti study how a network of wind turbines stays synchronized when hit by strong disturbances. Wind variability enters through an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck random process, and each turbine follows a Kuramoto-type equation. Stability is judged by the basin of attraction, the set of starting states that settle into sync. Simulations show sync depends on inertia, damping, wind speed, fluctuation rate, correlation time, and coupling strength.
arxiv-2605-25392: Samuel Drapeau and colleagues explain onshore-offshore renminbi forward disagreement despite linked spot prices. China runs a deliverable offshore market alongside a segmented onshore market, creating two venues for claims on one currency. In a joint equilibrium model with transaction costs and segmented supply, a benchmark with common supply and fixed costs predicts the wrong gap sign. Adding random offshore stress, a jump in trading costs, flips the benchmark while keeping spot parity. That yields a semi-explicit account of the gap from offshore liquidity stress likelihood and severity.
arxiv-2605-25492: Yanhang Li, Zhichao Fan, and Zexin Zhuang show that safety rankings between foundation models can flip with harness configuration alone. Pairwise verdicts like A is safer than B read as quantitative judgments, but hinge on choices benchmark papers leave underspecified. The team proves a finite-envelope result linking a measured pairwise-disagreement rate to cases where a strict ordering admits a configuration-pair reversal. A commit-stamped evaluation protocol operationalizes it. On every benchmark tested, configuration choice alone flips the pairwise verdict, isolating this strict-reversal failure mode.
arxiv-2605-25592: Lee and Oh study optimal design for multinomial logit bandits, where an agent picks a subset of items and observes a choice. The combinatorial action space makes design and subset optimization intractable. One is a design oracle written as a zero-one mixed-integer linear program with solver-certified early stopping. The other is a polynomial-time lifted design built on a tractable surrogate. They prove near G-optimality guarantees with the Kiefer-Wolfowitz equivalence theorem, and their best-assortment method carries a sample complexity bound.
arxiv-2605-25792: Ning, Liu, Zhang and Zhang build a flux-controlled anomalous Floquet quantum walk, realized in a driven bipartite lattice. One evolution operator rules quasienergy bands, boundary modes and bulk dynamics. Chirality gives the zero and pi gaps distinct topological information, forming trivial, zero-only, pi-only and coexistence sectors. In that sector a zero mode and a pi mode share one edge, spanning a boundary logical subspace. Bulk probes track the two winding numbers.
arxiv-2605-26092: Xiang, Luo and Wang tackle ultra-low-bit quantisation for large models on edge devices. Dense multiply-accumulate arrays strain memory and timing, while power-of-two quantisation swaps products for bit shifts. Its uneven lattice blurs angular detail below four bits. GoQuant reframes quantisation as dual-basis projection, building a sharper residual lattice with shift-and-add products. Its analytic solver skips gradient or iterative search. A data-free mode quantises LLaMA-2-7B in 0.47 minutes, a refined mode in about 4.4 minutes.
arxiv-2605-26492: Sil Hamilton and David Mimno diagnose why language-model stories feel so samey. From 20,000 stories across four models and five prompts, they find just 11 words in 88.3 percent of outputs, with little model variation. Repeat offenders include Elias, Mara, and Elara, lighthouse settings, and clockmaker and librarian professions. These tokens rarely appear in published literature or pretraining data, but turn up in preference data likely shared by all models. Oddly, such lighthouse tales are rarer than the typical post-training story, much of which leans on copyrighted characters or adult content.
arxiv-2605-26692: Yudai Suwa and Ken'ichiro Nakazato estimate when a newborn neutron star first grows a solid crust. A hot, lepton-rich protoneutron star cools by shedding neutrinos until heavy ions in its outer layers freeze. The pair use neutrino diffusion, entropy tracks, and a near-isentropic interior. They find when surface temperature first drops below the Coulomb freezing threshold at surface density. For standard physics the first solid appears roughly 100 to 500 seconds after birth, giving a handy late-time benchmark for crust onset.
arxiv-2605-26992: Lin and four co-authors survey machine unlearning for vision-language models and test how robust forgetting really is. They sort existing methods, test them under varied prompt settings, and propose three attacks that try to revive forgotten knowledge through context prompting or later training. Tests show many methods stay weak, often hiding rather than fully erasing target knowledge. The study calls for more reliable ways to make models forget.
arxiv-2605-27092: Boiquaye and Twum show that a left chi-coalgebra fits a general theory of left chi-coalgebras. This extra structure sits on one coefficient used to build the cyclic operator for cyclic sets generalizing Loday's twisted nerve of a group. In the general case, they show the resulting cyclic operator requires the other coefficient to carry a crossed G-set structure. The note thus places a specific construction inside a broader framework, clarifying what structure each coefficient must carry.
arxiv-2605-27292: Mathieu Dagreou and colleagues design canaries for privacy auditing that stay detectable without interfering with each other. Their IBIS framework picks canaries by influence, then refines them with a penalty that pushes their embeddings apart. The result beats existing canary methods on audit scores while cutting compute cost roughly a hundredfold.
arxiv-2605-27692: Leila Khatami and Tomaz Kosir classify every Jordan type found in a nilpotent matrix's commutator with hook-partition Jordan type. As a consequence, two partitions sharing one generic commuting Jordan type may still fail to commute with one another.
